And the coat of mail is maḥbūka because its rings are beaten out in streaks.» Zuhayr is describing a sandgrouse that fled from a falcon until it sought refuge from it in a nearby water; and before the verse:
حتى استغاثت بماء لا رشاء له ... من الأباطح في حافاته البرك
(Until it cried for help to a water with no rope, in the broad valleys, with al-burak on its banks.)
and after it:
كما استغاث بسيء فزّ غيطلة ... خاف العيون فلم ينظر به الحشك
(As the fawn of a thicket sought help in its mother's sīʾ-milk, fearing the watchers, and the udder-full one was not looked at.)
He says that this nearby water has no rope, i.e. no cord with which to draw from it, because it has no need of it; "min al-abāṭiḥ" means in wide, level places; "fī ḥāffātihi" means its sides; and al-burak is the plural of burka, a kind of water-bird. It crowns that water with the roots of the najm, i.e. the plant that has no stalk, and "tansijuhu" means bends it in an orderly bending like weaving, so it is an explicit metaphor. Al-kharīq is the cold, and the one fast in going; al-ḍāḥī is the ... [Translator's note: the source prints «الفاهر», apparently a corruption, perhaps for «الظاهر» "the exposed"; I read it so]; al-ḥubuk are the streaks in water when the wind strikes it, the plural of ḥabīka. Al-sayʾ, with fatḥa or kasra, is the milk at the tip of the udder; al-ghazz is the young of the wild cow; al-ghayṭala is the entangled trees, and al-ghazz was annexed to it because it is in it. Al-ʿuyūn here are the watchers of game. Ḥashakat al-durra bi-l-laban ḥashkan wa-ḥushūkan: the udder was full of milk; and in it is an indication that it was thirsty.
(الْخَرَّاصُونَ): the liars. Al-kharṣ is conjecture and guess; one says: "kam kharṣ arḍika?" (with kasra on the khāʾ), "what is the estimate of your land?". The origin of al-kharṣ is cutting, from their saying kharaṣa fulān kalāman wa-ikhtaraṣahu when he cut it off without a basis.
(غَمْرَةٍ): al-ghamra is from ghamarahu al-māʾ yaghmuruhu when it covered him; what is meant here is ignorance.

* I'rab:
(وَالذَّارِياتِ ذَرْواً): The wāw is a particle of oath and of genitive; الذاريات is genitive by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; ذروا is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), and the governor in it is the active participle, its object being omitted.
(فَالْحامِلاتِ وِقْراً): The fāʾ is a conjunction; الحاملات is conjoined to الذاريات; وقرا is the direct object of the participle. Whoever read it with fatḥa on the wāw regarded it as a maṣdar, built on naming the thing carried by it.
(فَالْجارِياتِ يُسْراً): The fāʾ is a conjunction; الجاريات is also conjoined to what precedes; يسرا is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl in Sībawayh's view, i.e. "a running possessing ease". It may also be parsed as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar which it has replaced, so it is an absolute object.
(فَالْمُقَسِّماتِ أَمْراً): The fāʾ is a conjunction; المقسمات is also conjoined; أمرا is the direct object of the participle.
(إِنَّما تُوعَدُونَ لَصادِقٌ): إن is a particle that resembles a verb; ما is a relative noun, its ism; the clause توعدون is the ṣila, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "you are promised it"; the lām is the shifted lām; صادق is the khabar of إن. ما may be a maṣdar, in which case ما and what is within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar which is the ism of إن, i.e. "what you are promised is true"; and the sentence has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath.
(وَإِنَّ الدِّينَ لَواقِعٌ): conjoined to what precedes.
(وَالسَّماءِ ذاتِ الْحُبُكِ): The wāw is a particle of oath and of genitive; السماء is genitive by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; ذات الحبك is an adjective of السماء.
(إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي قَوْلٍ مُخْتَلِفٍ): إن with its ism; the shifted lām; في قول is attached to an omitted khabar of إن; مختلف is an adjective of قول; and the sentence also has no position, because it is the answer to the oath.
(يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَنْ أُفِكَ): The pronoun refers to the Qur'an or to the Messenger, i.e. "he is turned away from it who is turned away", with the turning away than which there is none more severe or greater.
(قُتِلَ الْخَرَّاصُونَ): The sentence is an invocation, with no position; قتل is a passive past verb; الخراصون ... [Translator's note: the source here jumps without a break from the i'rab of «قتل الخراصون» (verse 10) directly to what are evidently words from verse 11 «الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ ساهُونَ», and the printed text reads «والخرّاصون وهم مبتدأ»; the omitted words are not supplied here]. ... and هم is a mubtadaʾ; في غمرة is attached to ساهون; ساهون is their khabar; and the nominal sentence has no position, because it is the ṣila of the relative.
(يَسْئَلُونَ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الدِّينِ): يسألون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the agent; أيان is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time, attached to an omitted advanced khabar; يوم الدين is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and the sentence is in the position of the accusative as the object of يسألون.
(يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ): يوم is an adverbial (mafʿūl fīhi) of time attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "it occurs" or "it comes"; هم is the mubtadaʾ and the clause يفتنون its khabar; على النار is attached to يفتنون, على having the sense of في; and the sentence is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of يوم to it. More on this i'rab will come in the section on benefits.
(ذُوقُوا فِتْنَتَكُمْ هذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ): The sentence is the content of an omitted saying, i.e. "and it is said to them at the time of punishment: taste". ذوقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the agent; فتنتكم is the direct object; هذا is the mubtadaʾ; الذي is a relative noun, its khabar; the clause كنتم is the ṣila; كان with its ism; به is attached to تستعجلون; and the clause تستعجلون is the khabar of كنتم.

* Rhetoric:
1- Kināya (metonymy) for the described thing: in His words «يؤفك عنه من أفك» there is a kināya for a described thing, namely the denier who rejects the truth. The pronoun in عنه refers to the Qur'an or to the Messenger, i.e. "he is turned away from it who is turned away, with a turning away than which there is none more severe or greater". It is also said that it refers to the Day of Resurrection. He swore by the scattering winds that the occurrence of the matter of the Resurrection is true; then He swore by the heaven that they are in conflicting speech about its occurrence, some of them doubting and some denying; then He said that he who is the one turned away is turned away from affirming the Day of Resurrection. The benefit of the kināya here is that when He specified this one as the one who is turned away, it conveyed that others are not turned away, as though He said: "turning away is truly established only for this one, and every turning away other than his is counted as non-existent in relation to it".
2- The implied metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): in His words «ذوقوا فتنتكم» He likened the punishment to food that is eaten, then omitted the thing likened to and borrowed for it something of its concomitants, namely tasting; its like has already preceded. It is also said that the original meaning of fitna is melting the ore so that its adulteration appears, then it was used for torment and burning. In al-Qāmūs: «al-fatn, with fatḥa, is the kind and the state, and from it "the life is fatnān", i.e. two colours, sweet and bitter; and the burning, and from it «على النار يفتنون».»

* Benefits:
Al-Zajjāj said: «يوم is accusative in two ways. One is that it is on the sense of "the recompense occurs on the day when they are tried over the Fire". The other is that its form is the form of the accusative while its meaning is the meaning of the nominative, because it is annexed to a sentence. You say "يعجبني يوم أنت قائم" and "يوم أنت تقوم": if you wish you put fatḥa, and if you wish you put ḍamma, as the poet said:
لم يمنع الشرب منها غير أن نطقت ... حمامة في غصون ذات أرقال
(Nothing prevented the drinking from it except that a dove cooed in branches that swayed.)
And it is narrated «غير أن نطقت» with ḍamma (on غير), since he annexed غير to أن, which is not firmly established, so he put fatḥa; and likewise when he annexed يوم to the sentence, he put fatḥa.»

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿وَبِٱلأَسْحَارِ هُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾: they pray.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿وَفِيۤ أَمْوَالِهِمْ حَقٌّ لَّلسَّآئِلِ وَٱلْمَحْرُومِ﴾.
As for «السائل» (the one who asks), it is the one who goes round from door to door; as for «المحروم» (the deprived), it is the one denied his livelihood (al-muḥāraf), or the one who has no share in the spoils.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿وَفِي ٱلأَرْضِ آيَاتٌ لِّلْمُوقِنِينَ﴾.
The signs of the earth are its mountains, the variety of its plants and its rivers, and the creatures that are in it.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿وَفِيۤ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾.
There are signs too: one of you eats and drinks through a single entrance and excretes from two places. Then He rebuked them, saying: ﴿أَفَلاَ تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ (Will you not then see?)

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿فَوَرَبِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
He, Mighty and Majestic, swore by Himself that what I have told you is truly the truth, just as (مثل ما أنكم) you speak. Someone may ask: how have «ما» and «أنّ» come together, when one of them suffices for the other? There are two answers to this. The first is that the Arabs combine two things, both among nouns and among particles (adawāt), when their wording differs. Among nouns there is the poet's saying:
من النّفر اللائى الذين إذا همُ * يَهاب اللئامُ حلقهَ البابِ قَعْقَعوا
(Of the band who — who, when the base fear the door-knocker, rattle it.) So he combined «اللائى» and «الذين», though each of them suffices for the other.
As for particles, there is the saying:
ما إِنْ رأيتُ ولا سمعت به * كاليوم طالى أيْنُق جُرْب
(I have never seen nor heard of anything like today: one tarring mangy she-camels.) So he combined «ما» and «إن», both of which are negations (jaḥd), one of which suffices for the other.
As for the other answer: if the meaning had been expressed with «ما» alone, it would be as though speech in itself were true and not a lie, and that is not what was meant. What they meant is only that it is true just as it is true that a human being speaks.
Do you not see that your saying «أحقٌّ منطقك» (Is your speech true?) means: is it true or a lie? And that your saying «أحقٌّ أنك تنطق؟» (Is it true that you speak?) means: does speech belong to man and not to others? So you introduced «أنَّ» in order to distinguish thereby between the two meanings. This is the one of the two answers I prefer.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read (مثلَ) in the nominative (rafʿ), while the people of the Ḥijāz and al-Ḥasan read it in the accusative (naṣb). Whoever read it in the nominative made it a naʿt (adjective) of «الحق»; whoever read it in the accusative put it in the manner of the maṣdar (verbal noun), as when you say: «إنه لحق حقا» (It is truly true). And the Arabs put it in the accusative even when the noun is made nominative by it, saying: «مثلَ من عبدالله؟» (Like whom is ʿAbd Allāh?), and they say: «عبدالله [185/ا] مثلَك» (ʿAbd Allāh is like you), and «أنت مثلَه» (You are like him). The reason for its accusative is that the kāf (of comparison) may enter upon it, so it is put in the accusative when the kāf is dropped. If someone asks: may one then say «زيدٌ الأسدَ شدةً» (Zayd is the lion in strength), putting «الأسد» in the accusative when you drop the kāf? I say: no; that is because «مثلَ» stands in place of the kāf, whereas «الأسد» does not stand in place of it. Do you not see, in the poet's saying:
وزعتُ بكالهراوة أعوجِىٍّ * إذا وَنتِ الرِّكاب جرى وثابا
(I held them back on one like a cudgel, an Aʿwajī steed, who, when the riding camels flag, runs leaping.)
that the kāf has sufficed in place of «مثل»? And the Arabs combine the two, saying: «زيد كمثلك» (Zayd is like the like of you); and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿ليس كمثله شىء وهو السميع البصير﴾. Their coming together is evidence that their meaning is one, just as I told you about «ما» and «إن» and «لا» and others.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾.
The Prophet ﷺ did not know of it until Allah revealed it to him.
And His saying: ﴿ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ﴾.
He honoured them by the deed that brought him near.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ﴾.
It is nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied pronoun: «أنتم قوم منكرون» (You are a people unknown).
This is said by Abraham, peace be upon him, to the angels.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ﴾.
He returned to them. Although «الروغ» has this meaning, it is not used unless the one doing it conceals his going [or his coming]. Do you not see that you do not say «قد راغ أهل مكة» (the people of Mecca have slipped away) when you mean they returned or came back? But if a returner concealed his return, «راغ» and «يروغ» would be fitting for it.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلاَمٍ عَلَيمٍ﴾.
That is, when he grows up. One of our elders used to say: when knowledge is still awaited [for one] who is described by it, you say of the «عليم» who does not yet know: «إنه لعالم عن قيل» (he will be knowing shortly) and «فاقِهٌ» (understanding); of the lord («السيد»): «سائد», and of the generous («الكريم»): «كارم». What he said is good, and this is good Arabic speech; yet Allah has said it with «عليم», «حليم» and «ميت».
The elders used to say of one who has not yet died but will die: «هو مائت عن قليل» (he will be dying shortly); but the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more correct than their saying. Among what they adduced as evidence is the poet's saying:
كريم كصفو الماء ليس بباخل * بشىء، ولا مهد ملاما لباخل
(Generous, like clear water, not stingy with anything, nor one who directs blame at a stingy man.)
He means «بخيل» (stingy), but he made it «باخل» because he has not yet been stingy.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَقْبَلَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُهُ فِي صَرَّةٍ﴾.
In a cry. She did not come forward from one place to another; it is only like your saying: «أقبل يشتمنى» (he set about insulting me), i.e. he began insulting me. They have mentioned that the cry was «أوَّه» (Ah!), and some said it was «يا ويلتا» (Woe is me!).
And His saying: ﴿فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا﴾.
Like this, that is, she gathered her fingers and struck her forehead; ﴿وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ﴾: will a barren old woman give birth? You make it nominative by the implied (verb) «تلد».
«[Translator's note: the source has «بالضيمر», evidently a slip for «بالضمير» (by the implied element).]»

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتَرَكْنَا فِيهَآ آيَةً﴾.
Its meaning is: We left it as a sign; just as you say of the sky «فيها آية» (in it is a sign), meaning that it is itself the sign.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿فَتَوَلَّىٰ بِرُكْنِهِ﴾.
It is said: «تولى» means he turned away from the Reminder by the strength he had in himself; and it is said: «فتولى بركنه» means with those who were with him, because they were his strength.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ﴾.
He did what deserves blame; one says «قد ألام» (he has become blameworthy). And His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ كَانَ فِى يُوسُفَ وَإِخْوَتِهِ آياتٌ لِلسّائِلِينَ﴾: they are the signs, they and their deeds.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كَٱلرَّمِيمِ﴾.
«الرميم» is the vegetation of the earth when it dries and withers (dabisa); then it is «رميم».

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿تَمَتَّعُواْ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ﴾.
That «حين» (period) was three days.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلصَّاعِقَةُ﴾.
The generality of readers read it [الصاعقة] with the alif.
He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ told me, from al-Suddī, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, that he read (الصَّعقة) without the alif, «وهم ينظرون».

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَمَا ٱسْتَطَاعُواْ مِن قِيَامٍ﴾.
He is saying: they did not stand up against it. Had it been «فما استطاعُوا من إقامةٍ», it would have been correct.
Dropping the alif from it is like His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿والله أَنْبَتَكُم مِنَ الأَرْضِ نَبَاتاً﴾; had it been «إنباتا», it would have been correct.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ﴾.
The readers put it in the accusative [55/ا], except al-Aʿmash and his companions, who put it in the genitive (khafḍ), because in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, as far as I know, it is: «وفى قوم نوح» (and in the people of Noah).
Whoever puts it in the accusative does so in one of two ways: the thunderbolt seized them and seized the people of Noah;
or, if you wish: We destroyed them and destroyed the people of Noah. There is another way, no less dear to me than these two: that you imply a verb — «and mention to them the people of Noah» — as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ﴾ and ﴿وَنُوحاً إِذْ نَادَى مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ in many places in the Qurʾān, its meaning being: inform them and mention to them the prophets and their stories.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿بِأَييْدٍ﴾: with strength.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ﴾, that is: We are possessed of ample means for Our creation. Likewise His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ﴾.
«[Translator's note: the source has «لدو», evidently for «لذو» (possessors of).]»

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَمِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ﴾.
The pairs among all animals are the male and the female; and among other things: the different colours of plants and the tastes of fruits, some sweet and some sour — those are two pairs.

farraa:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿فَفِرُّوۤاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Its meaning is: flee to Him, to obedience to Him, away from disobeying Him.

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿أَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِهِ﴾.
Its meaning is: did the people of Mecca [55/ب] and the past nations bequeath it to one another, since they said to you what the nations said to their messengers?

farraa:56-56.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقْتُ ٱلْجِنَّ وَٱلإِنسَ إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُونِ﴾.
Except that they should affirm My oneness; and this is specific. He is saying: I did not create the people of felicity among the two groups except that they should affirm My oneness.
Some said: He created them so that they would do (this); some of them did and some left it. There is no argument in it for the people of qadar (the Qadarites); and it has (already) been explained.

farraa:57-58.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿مَآ أُرِيدُ مِنْهُم مِّن رِّزْقٍ﴾.
He is saying: I do not want them to provide for themselves; ﴿وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَن يُطْعِمُونِ﴾: that they should feed any of My creation. ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلْقُوَّةِ ٱلْمَتِينُ﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read (المتين) in the genitive, making it a naʿt (adjective) of «القوة»; even though it is feminine in form, he took it in the sense of the rope and of a twisted thing.
One of the Arabs recited:
لكل دَهْرٍ قد لَبِسْتُ أثْوباً * من ريطةٍ وَاليُمنَةَ المُعَصَّبا
(For every age I have worn garments: of fine sheets, and the striped Yemeni cloth.) He made «المُعَصَّب» a naʿt of «اليُمْنَة», which is feminine in form, because «اليُمنة» is a kind and type of garment, namely embroidered cloth (al-washy), so he took it in that sense.
The people read (المتينُ) in the nominative, as a description of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

farraa:59-59.t:
His saying [56/ا], Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ ذَنُوباً﴾.
«الذنوب» in the speech of the Arabs is the large bucket, but the Arabs take it in the sense of share and portion.
The exegesis came in that sense: those who did wrong will have a portion of punishment, as befell those before them. The poet said:
لنَا ذَنوبٌ وَلكمْ ذَنوبُ * فإنْ أبيتمْ فلنا القَليبُ
(We have a bucketful and you have a bucketful; if you refuse, then the well is ours.)
«الذنوب» is treated as both masculine and feminine.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَٱلذَّارِيَاتِ ذَرْواً﴾.
He means: the winds.

farraa:2-2.t: ﴿فَٱلْحَامِلاَتِ وِقْراً﴾: He means: the clouds, because they carry the water.

farraa:3-4.t:
﴿فَٱلْجَارِيَاتِ يُسْراً﴾: they are the ships that run with ease. ﴿فَٱلْمُقَسِّمَاتِ أَمْراً﴾: the angels who come with differing commands: Gabriel, master of severity (ghilẓa), Michael, master of mercy, and the Angel of Death, who comes with death. That is the apportioning of affairs.
«[Translator's note: the source has «الغلطة» ("error"), evidently for «الغلظة» ("severity"); translated as "severity".]»

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلْحُبُكِ﴾.
Al-ḥubuk is the rippling of anything, like the sand when a gentle wind passes over it, and standing water when the wind passes over it; and the coat of mail, the iron coat of mail, also has ḥubuk; and the curly hair, its waves are ḥubuk. The singular of ḥubuk is ḥibāk and ḥabīka.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي قَوْلٍ مُّخْتَلِفٍ﴾.
The answer to the oath. The differing speech is the denial by some of them of the Qurʾān and of Muḥammad, and the faith of others.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَنْ أُفِكَ﴾.
He means: he is turned away from the Qurʾān and faith who is turned away, as He said: ﴿أَجِئْتَنَا لِتَأْفِكَنَا﴾: he says: to turn us away from our gods and to bar us.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿قُتِلَ ٱلْخَرَّاصُونَ﴾.
He says: cursed be the liars who said that Muḥammad, Allah bless him, is mad, a poet, a liar, a sorcerer. They conjectured (kharraṣū) about what they had no knowledge of.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ﴾.
"When is the Day of Judgement?" Allah said: ﴿يوم الدّين. يَوْمَ هُمْ على النارِ يُفْتَنُون﴾. You put (يومَ هُمْ) in the accusative only because you annexed it to two things [i.e. a nominal clause]. When "day" and "night" are annexed to a noun that has a verb [i.e. a predicate], and both are nominative, "day" is accusative, even if it is in the position of the genitive or the nominative. When it is annexed to faʿala or yafʿalu or the like, then its nominative in the position of the nominative, and its genitive in the position of the genitive, are allowed. So had it been said: يومُ هم على النار يفتنون, putting يوم in the nominative, it would have been a valid view, but none of the readers read it so.

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿يُفْتَنُونَ﴾: they are burned and punished with the Fire.

farraa:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿ذُوقُواْ فِتْنَتَكُمْ﴾: he says: taste your punishment which you used to seek to hasten in the world.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿آخِذِينَ﴾ and "وفاكهين".
They are accusative by detachment (qaṭʿ, i.e. as ḥāl); and had they been [184/b] nominative, it would have been correct: their nominative being as a khabar (predicate); and another nominative is also [possible] by resumption (istiʾnāf).

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿كَانُواْ قَلِيلاً مِّن ٱللَّيْلِ مَا يَهْجَعُونَ﴾.
If you wish, you put ما in the position of the nominative, and the meaning is: their slumber was little. Al-hujūʿ is sleep.
And if you wish, you make ما a connective (ṣila) with no position, and put قليلا in the accusative by يهجعون, meaning: they used to sleep a little of the night.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: (والذاريات ذروا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is for the oath, and what is sworn by (muqsam bihi) is genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied "I swear". «ذَرْوًا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) governed by its derivative, namely the active participle; the object is omitted by restriction (iqtiṣār), since there is no counterpart to what it scatters here.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: His words «فالحاملات»: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «الذاريات»; «وِقْرا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «الحاملات».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «يسرا» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); its adjective has taken its place, i.e. "a running with ease".

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: (إنما توعدون لصادق) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the answer to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: (وإن الدين لواقع) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the answer to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «والسماء»: sworn by (muqsam bihi), attached to (mutaʿalliq) "I swear"; «ذات» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: (إنكم لفي قول مختلف) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «يؤفك» is an adjective (ṣifa) of {قَوْلٍ}; «مَنْ» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: (قتل الخراصون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective); «ساهون» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «يسألون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from {الْخَرَّاصُونَ}. «أيان» is an interrogative noun, an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) a khabar (predicate) placed first; «يوم» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «أيان يوم الدين» is the object of the asking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: «يوم» is the object of an implied "I mean"; the preposition «على النار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُفْتنون», which carries the implied meaning of "they are exposed".

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «ذوقوا» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying) of an implied saying, and the clause «هذا الذي» is resumptive within the scope of the saying. The preposition «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تستعجلون».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: (إن المتقين في جنات وعيون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «آخذين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of being (istiqrār) in the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ»; «ما» is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle. The clause «إنهم كانوا» is resumptive; «قبل» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of «كان».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «كانوا» is a badal (substitute) from the earlier {كَانُوا}; the clause «يهجعون» is the khabar (predicate) of «كان»; «ما» is redundant (zāʾida), and «قليلا» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the implied form being "they used to sleep, of the night, a little sleep".

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: (وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يستغفرون», and the clause «هم يستغفرون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {يَهْجَعُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The preposition «للسائل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «حق», and the clause «وفي أموالهم حق» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {هُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: (وفي الأرض آيات للموقنين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; the preposition «للموقنين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آيات».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The preposition «وفي أنفسكم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to {وَفِي الأَرْضِ} and is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what that is attached to; the clause «أفلا تبصرون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «وفي السماء رزقكم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «في الأرض آيات»; «ما» is a relative noun conjoined to «رزقكم».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause «إنه لحق» is the answer to the oath. «مثل» is a naʿt (adjective) of «حق», made indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is annexed to an indeclinable word; «ما» is redundant (zāʾida), and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: «المكرمين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «ضيف», and «ضيف» is singular with a plural meaning.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: «إذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) {حَدِيثُ}, i.e. "has their story reached you, occurring at the time they entered upon him?" «سلاما» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "we greet with a greeting". «سلام» is mubtadaʾ (subject) with an implied khabar (predicate), i.e. "peace be upon you". «قوم» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "you".

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The clause «فراغ» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {قَالَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The preposition «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «خيفة». The clause «فأوجس» is resumptive, as is the clause «قالوا», and the clause «وبشَّروه» is a ḥāl.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «فأقبلت» is resumptive; the preposition «في صرة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «امرأته»; the clause «فصكَّت» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «أقبلت». «عجوز» is the khabar (predicate) of an implied «أنا», and «وعقيم» is a second khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: (كذلك قال ربك) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The kāf stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "He said a saying like that saying". The clause «قال» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying), and the clause «إنه هو الحكيم» is resumptive; «هو» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: (فما خطبكم أيها المرسلون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The fāʾ connects (rābiṭa) to the apodosis (jawāb) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have been sent for a matter, then what is your business?" «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «خطبكم» is its khabar (predicate). The clause «أيها المرسلون» is resumptive within the scope of the saying, and «المرسلون» is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The genitive maṣdar (verbal noun) «لنرسل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {أُرْسِلْنَا}; the preposition «من طين» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «حجارة».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: «مسومة» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {حِجَارَةً}; «عند» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مسومة», as is «للمسرفين».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The clause «فأخرجنا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {أُرْسِلْنَا} in verse (32); the preposition «من المؤمنين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun that is the noun (ism) of «كان».

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «فما وجدنا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «أخرجنا»; «غير» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the preposition «من المسلمين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «غير».

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The clause «وتركنا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «ما وجدنا»; the preposition «للذين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آية».

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The preposition «وفي موسى» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the preposition {فِيهَا} in the previous verse, with the preposition repeated because what it is conjoined to is a genitive pronoun; so it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what that is attached to. «إذ» is an adverbial noun, a badal (substitute) of inclusion (ishtimāl) from «موسى». The preposition «بسلطان» is attached to «أرسلناه».

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The clause «فَتَوَلَّى» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {أَرْسَلْنَاهُ}; the preposition «بركنه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تولى»; «ساحر» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "he". «أو» is for doubt: he put himself — although he knew him to be a prophet — in the position of one doubting his matter, to deceive his people.

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The clause «فأخذناه» is resumptive; «جنوده» is a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the hāʾ; and the clause «وهو مليم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «أخذناه».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The preposition «وفي عاد» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «في موسى» in verse (38); «إذ» is an adverbial noun, a badal (substitute) of inclusion (ishtimāl) from «عاد».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: The clause «ما تذر» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from {الرِّيحَ}; «شيء» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); the clause «أتت» is a naʿt (adjective) of «شيء»; the clause «جَعَلَتْه» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «تذر»; and the preposition «كالرميم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: «وفي ثمود» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «في عاد» in verse (41); «إذ» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (ishtimāl) from «ثمود». The nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «قيل» is the pronoun of the maṣdar (verbal noun). «حتى» is a particle of limit and of the genitive, and «حين» is a genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The clause «فعتوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {قِيلَ}, and the clause «وهم ينظرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The clause «فما استطاعوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «أخذتهم»; «قيام» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and «من» is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: His words «وقوم»: the object of an implied «أهلكنا», and the clause of the implied verb is resumptive; the preposition «من قبل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied verb; and the clause «إنهم كانوا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قوم نوح».

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: His words «والسماء»: accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb explained by what follows it, and the implied clause is resumptive; the clause «بنيناها» is explicative. The preposition «بأيد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «بنيناها», and the clause «وإنَّا لموسعون» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «بنيناها».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: His words «والأرض»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it, and the implied clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the implied clause «بنيناها»; the clause «فرشناها» is explicative. The clause «فنعم الماهدون» is conjoined to the clause «فرشناها», and the one specified [for praise] by «نعم» is omitted, i.e. "We".

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: (ومن كل شيء خلقنا زوجين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is conjunctive, and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خلقنا»; the clause «خَلَقْنا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the implied clause «فرشنا», and the clause «لعلكم تذكرون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The clause «ففروا» is resumptive, as is the clause «إني ... نذير»; the two prepositions are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نذير»; «مبين» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The clause «ولا تجعلوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «فِرُّوا»; «مع» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object; «آخر» is a naʿt (adjective) of «إلها»; and the clause «إني ... نذير» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: (كذلك ما أتى الذين من قبلهم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The kāf is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the matter is thus", and the clause is resumptive, as is the clause «ما أتى»; «رسول» is the fāʿil (agent) and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «قالوا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الذين»; «ساحر» is the khabar of an implied «هو».

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: The clause «أتواصوا» is resumptive, as is the clause «هم قوم».

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The clause «تَوَلَّ» is resumptive; the clause «فما أنت بملوم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما».

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The clause «وذَكِّر» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «تَوَلَّ», and the clause «فإن الذكرى تنفع» is conjoined to the clause «ذكِّر».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The clause «وما خلقت» is resumptive; «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr). His words «ليعبدون»: the lām is causal; the verb is an imperfect, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أن», the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the nūn is that of protection (wiqāya), and the implied yāʾ is the object of the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The clause «ما أريد» is resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يطعمون» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); «ذو» is a second khabar (predicate); «المتين» is a third khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: The clause «فإن للذين» is resumptive; «مثل» is a naʿt (adjective), and «مثل» does not become definite through annexation. The clause «فلا يستعجلون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause, and «يستعجلون» is like {لِيَعْبُدُونِ}.

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: The clause «فويل» is resumptive; «ويل» is mubtadaʾ (subject), and beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it expresses an imprecation. The preposition «من يومهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ويل»; «الذي» is a naʿt of «يومهم».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He, والذاريات فَالْحَامِلَات فالجاريان فَالْمُقَسِّمَات: all of these are adjectives standing in place of a described thing sworn by, on the assumption of the oath being by its Creator and Mover, who is Allah, there is no god but He. Its implied form is "By the Lord of the winds that scatter, then the clouds that carry a load, then the ships that run, then the angels that apportion" (ورب الرياح الذاريات فالسحاب الحاملات وقرا فالسفن الجاريات فالملائكة المقسمات). And the answer [to the oath] is إنما توعدون لصادق. [Translator's note: «فالجاريان» is as printed in the edition; the Quranic word is فالجاريات.]

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying يسرا: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "an easy running" (جريا يسرا).

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying يَوْم هم على النَّار يفتنون: يوم is indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because its annexation is not genuine (ghayr maḥḍa), since it is annexed to something not fully declinable (ghayr mutamakkin). Its position is accusative in the sense of "the recompense is on the day they are tried over the Fire" (الجزاء يوم هم على النار يفتنون). It is also said that its position is nominative as a badal (substitute) of يوم الدين. It is also said that it is accusative and not indeclinable, and its accusative is by an implied [word], its implied form being "the recompense is on the day they..." (الجزاء يوم هم).

mekki-muskil:17-17.t:
His saying كَانُوا قَلِيلا من اللَّيْل مَا يهجعون: the noun of كان is the latent pronoun in it, which is the wāw; يهجعون is the khabar (predicate) of كان; and قليلا is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or of an omitted adverb, its implied form being "they used to sleep a little time" (كانوا وقتا قليلا يهجعون) or "they used to sleep a little sleep" (هجوعا قليلا يهجعون); and ما is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis.
If you wish, you may make ما together with the verb a maṣdar in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) of the latent pronoun in كان, with قليلا as the khabar of كان; its implied form is "their sleeping at night was little" (كان هجوعهم من الليل قليلا). If you wish, you may make the maṣdar nominative by قليل [as its agent] and put قليلا in the accusative as the khabar of كان.
It is not permissible to make قليلا accusative by يهجعون unless ما is redundant, because if you made it accusative by يهجعون while ما with the verb is a maṣdar, you would have put the ṣila (relative clause) before the relative.
It is also possible that قليلا is the khabar of كان, its noun being in it, and ما negating; this is the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and pausing on قليلا is then good; it is the view of Yaʿqūb and others. One does not pause on قليل on the earlier views.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t:
His saying {إِنَّه لحق مثل مَا أَنكُمْ تنطقون}: whoever reads مثلَ in the accusative made it indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its annexation to something not fully declinable (ghayr mutamakkin), namely أنكم, with ما redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. It is also said that it is indeclinable on the fatḥa because مثل and ما are one noun; when the two were made one thing, مثل was made indeclinable on the fatḥa; this is the view of al-Māzinī. It is also said that مثلا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of an indefinite, namely لحق; this is the view of al-Jarmī. It is also said that it is a ḥāl of the nominative latent pronoun in His saying لحق, with ما redundant and مثل annexed to أنكم; it did not take full declension because of its annexation to something not fully declinable, and it is a non-genuine annexation. Some of the Kufans said مثل is accusative by the omission of the كاف, its implied form being "it is truly real, like what you speak" (إنه لحق كمثل ما أنكم تنطقون), with ما redundant, its implied form being "like your speaking" (كمثل نطقكم); and that is not permissible according to the Basrans. Abū Muḥammad [i.e. Makkī] said: whoever reads the accusative, it is possible that it is by way of emphasis, in the sense "it is truly real, as real as your speaking" (إنه لحق حقا مثل نطقكم).
As for whoever reads مثلُ in the nominative, he made it an adjective of حق, because it is indefinite, since its annexation is not genuine, because the respects in which likeness occurs between two things that resemble each other are many; therefore it did not become definite by its annexation to أنكم. Since it did not become definite, it was good to describe حق with it, just as you say مررت برجل مثلك ("I passed by a man like you"). On these views أنكم is in the position of the genitive by مثل, and it together with what follows it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); the implied form is "it is truly real, like your speaking" (إنه لحق مثل نطقكم).

mekki-muskil:25-25.t:
His saying قَالُوا سَلاما: سلام is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), or because the saying falls upon it [as its object].
His saying قَالَ سَلام: a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) omitted, its implied form being "he said: peace be upon you" (قال سلام عليكم). It is also said that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "my affair is peace" (أمري سلام). Whoever reads سِلْم takes it on the assumption "we are peace(ful)" (نحن سلم); it is also said that it means سلام, just as one says حِلّ and حلال with the same meaning.
His saying وَقَالَت عَجُوز عقيم: عجوز is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "I am an old woman" (أنا عجوز).

mekki-muskil:46-46.t: His saying وَقوم نوح: whoever reads قوم in the genitive conjoins it to His saying وفي عاد إذ أرسلنا; it is also said that it is conjoined to وفي موسى; and it is also said: to وفي الأرض. Whoever reads it in the accusative conjoins it to the هاء and the ميم in His saying فأخذتهم; it is also said that its implied form is "and We destroyed the people of Noah" (وأهلكنا قوم نوح); it is also said: in the sense of "and remember the people of Noah" (واذكر قوم نوح); it is also said that it is conjoined to فأخذناه; and it is also said: to فنبذناهم.

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying كَذَلِك مَا أَتَى: the كاف is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the matter is thus" (الأمر كذلك). It is also said that it is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:58-58.t: His saying المتين: a khabar (predicate) after a khabar of إنّ. It is also said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of الرزاق, or of ذو القوة, or [nominative] by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or a naʿt of the noun of إنّ according to its position. Whoever reads it in the genitive makes it a naʿt of القوة, and it is masculine because [القوة] is not a real feminine.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t: ﴿وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; وبالأسحار: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يستغفرون﴾, and the bāʾ has the meaning of «في» (in); هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause يستغفرون is the khabar (predicate). What is attached to the khabar was placed first because it is permissible to place the governing word (al-ʿāmil) first.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وفي أموالهم حق للسائل والمحروم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; وفي أموالهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); حق is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); وللسائل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective); والمحروم is conjoined to السائل. The clause is conjoined to the khabar of kāna, so it is a third khabar.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿وفي الأرض آيات للموقنين﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, or resumptive; وفي الأرض is a fronted khabar (predicate); وآيات is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); وللموقنين is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿آيات﴾. The clause ﴿وفي الأرض...﴾ is conjoined, or resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿وفي أنفسكم أفلا تبصرون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; وفي أنفسكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) whose mubtadaʾ (subject) has been omitted, the implied form being: آيات (signs). The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī); the fāʾ is conjunctive, conjoining to an omitted, implied clause; لا is negating; and تبصرون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive. وفي السماء: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). ورزقكم is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). The wāw is conjunctive. ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun conjoined to ﴿رزقكم﴾, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿توعدون﴾ is an imperfect verb, passive (built for the one whose agent is not named). The wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The clause ﴿توعدون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) is omitted.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t: ﴿فورب السماء والأرض إنه لحق مثل ما أنكم تنطقون﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive. The wāw: a particle of oath and of the genitive. ﴿رب﴾ is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being: أقسم (I swear). ﴿السماء﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the kasra. ﴿الأرض﴾ is conjoined to السماء. ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun. The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿حق﴾ is its khabar (predicate). ﴿مثل﴾ is indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حق﴾; the reason for its indeclinability is that it is annexed to an indeclinable word. ﴿ما﴾ is an indefinite noun that is qualified (nakira mawṣūfa), in the position of the genitive by annexation to مثل. ﴿أن﴾ is an abrogating particle. ﴿كم﴾ is the noun of inna. The clause ﴿تنطقون﴾ is its khabar. The clause ﴿أنكم﴾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation; or ﴿ما﴾ is a qualified indefinite noun and the clause is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: هو أنكم (it is that you…).

muyesser-irab:24-24.t: ﴿هل أتاك حديث ضيف إبراهيم المكرمين﴾: هل is an interrogative particle; أتاك is a verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ضيف إبراهيم is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and المكرمين is a naʿt (adjective) of ضيف. [Translator's note: the source does not parse حديث, the fāʿil (agent) of أتاك; ضيف is the muḍāf ilayhi of حديث, and إبراهيم the muḍāf ilayhi of ضيف.]

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿إذ﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) for past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حديث﴾ or to ﴿المكرمين﴾ in the previous ayah.
﴿دخلوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿دخلوا﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it.
﴿عليه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿دخلوا﴾.
﴿فقالوا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause ﴿قالوا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿دخلوا﴾.
﴿سلامًا﴾: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: نسلِّم سلاما (we greet with a greeting of peace).
﴿قال﴾: a past verb, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: هو (he).
﴿سلام﴾: a mubtadaʾ (subject); it was permissible to begin with it although it is indefinite because it carries the meaning of a supplication; the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: سلام عليكم (peace be upon you).
﴿قوم﴾: the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: وأنتم (and you are), or هم (they are).
﴿منكرون﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t: ﴿فراغ إلى أهله فجاء بعجل سمين﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, conjoining to an implied clause that the context requires, i.e.: so he hastened to honour them without letting them notice; راغ is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); وإلى أهله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) راغ; فجاء is conjoined, expressing immediate sequence (al-taʿqīb); وبعجل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جاء; and سمين is a naʿt (adjective) of عجل.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t: ﴿فقربه إليهم قال ألا تأكلون﴾: conjoined to what preceded; وإليهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) قربه; ألا is an interrogative particle [Translator's note: i.e. its hamza], and لا is negating, and the interrogative is for offering (al-ʿarḍ) or for disapproval (al-inkār); تأكلون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); and the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying).

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿فأوجس منهم خيفة﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, conjoining to an implied clause that the context requires; أوجس is a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being هو (he); and خيفة is the object (mafʿūl) of أوجس.
﴿قالوا لا تخف وبشروه بغلام عليم﴾: لا is the prohibitive lā, and تخف is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾; بشروه is a past verb, a fāʿil, and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وبغلام: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بشروه﴾; and عليم is a naʿt (adjective) of غلام.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t: ﴿فأقبلت امرأته في صرة فصكت وجهها وقالت عجوز عقيم﴾: also conjoined to an implied clause that cannot be done without; امرأته is the fāʿil (agent) of فأقبلت; وفي صرة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); فصكت is conjoined to ﴿فأقبلت﴾; ووجهها is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وقالت is also conjoined; عجوز is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. أنا عجوز (I am an old woman); and عقيم is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:30-30.t: ﴿قالوا كذلك قال ربك إنه هو الحكيم العليم﴾: قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: a saying like that which we said; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; ﴿قال ربك﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun; هو is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position; الحكيم is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and العليم is a second khabar of inna.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t: ﴿قال فما خطبكم أيها المرسلون﴾: قال is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), i.e. Ibrāhīm; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); ما is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); خطبكم is the khabar (predicate); ﴿أي﴾ is the one addressed (munādā) from which the vocative particle has been omitted, and it is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is a specifically intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda); ها is for alerting (al-tanbīh); and المرسلون is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أي﴾.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t: ﴿قالوا إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم مجرمين﴾: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; أرسل is a past verb, passive (built for the one whose agent is not named), and نا is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause أرسلنا is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and inna together with what falls in its scope is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying); وإلى قوم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أرسلنا﴾; and مجرمين is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:33-33.t: ﴿لنرسل عليهم حجارة من طين﴾: the lām is for causation (al-taʿlīl); نرسل is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit أن after the lām of causation, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: نحن (we); وعليهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نرسل; حجارة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من طين is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حجارة﴾; and the lām of causation together with what it governs is attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t: ﴿مسومة عند ربك للمسرفين﴾: مسومة is a second naʿt (adjective) of حجارة, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, because it has been qualified by the preposition and its genitive noun; عند ربك: the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مسومة﴾; and وللمسرفين: a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to ﴿مسومة﴾.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t: ﴿فأخرجنا من كان فيها من المؤمنين﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it discloses clauses that have been omitted; أخرجنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); من is an object (mafʿūl); كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: هم (they); فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna; من المؤمنين is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause of kāna is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The pronoun in His words فيها refers back to the towns of the people of Lūṭ.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t: ﴿فما وجدنا فيها غير بيت من المسلمين﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; ما is negating; وجدنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); غير بيت is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and من المسلمين is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:37-37.t: ﴿وتركنا فيها آية للذين يخافون العذاب الأليم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; تركنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); وفيها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تركنا﴾; آية is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); للذين is a naʿt (adjective) of آية; and the clause ﴿يخافون العذاب الأليم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t: ﴿وفي موسى إذ أرسلناه إلى فرعون بسلطان مبين﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿في موسى﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, conjoined to ﴿فيها﴾ in the words of Allah the Exalted ﴿وتركنا فيها آية﴾ with the preposition repeated, so the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تركنا﴾ in terms of meaning, and the implied form is: and We left in the story of Mūsā a sign; ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) for past time, attached to ﴿تركنا﴾; the clause ﴿أرسلناه﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿إلى فرعون﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾; ﴿بسلطان﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: مؤيّدًا (supported); and ﴿مبين﴾ is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:39-39.t: ﴿فتولى بركنه وقال ساحر أو مجنون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; تولى is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring back to Firʿawn; بركنه is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of Firʿawn; قال is conjoined to تولى; ساحر is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: هو ساحر (he is a sorcerer); أو is a conjunction for leaving the matter vague to the listener (al-ibhām), or for doubt; and مجنون is conjoined to ساحر.

muyesser-irab:40-40.t: ﴿فأخذناه وجنوده فنبذناهم في اليم وهو مليم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; أخذناه is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); جنوده is conjoined to the object of أخذناه, and it has been said: it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). فنبذناهم في اليم is conjoined to أخذناه; وفي اليم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نبذناه [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the ayah is نبذناهم]. وهو: the wāw is circumstantial (of the ḥāl), and هو is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); مليم is the khabar (predicate); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of نبذناهم, or from the object of أخذناه.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t: ﴿وفي عاد إذ أرسلنا عليهم الريح العقيم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿في عاد﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, conjoined to ﴿فيها﴾ in the words of Allah the Exalted ﴿وتركنا فيها آية﴾ with the preposition repeated, so the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تركنا﴾ in terms of meaning, and the implied form is: and We left in the story of ʿĀd a sign; ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) for past time, attached to ﴿تركنا﴾; the clause ﴿أرسلنا﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿عليهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾; ﴿الريح﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿العقيم﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of الريح.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t: ﴿ما تذر من شيء أتت عليه إلا جعلته كالرميم﴾: ما is negating; تذر is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: هي (it), i.e. the wind; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الريح; من is a redundant (ṣila) preposition, and شيء is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause أتت عليه is a naʿt (adjective) of شيء; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); جعلته is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause stands in the place of the second object of ﴿تذر﴾, as if it were said: it leaves nothing except made (into…); ﴿كالرميم﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as the second object of ﴿جعلته﴾, and ﴿الرميم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:43-43.t: ﴿وفي ثمود إذ قيل لهم تمتعوا حتى حين﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿في ثمود﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, conjoined to ﴿فيها﴾ in the words of Allah the Exalted ﴿وتركنا فيها آية﴾ with the preposition repeated, so the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تركنا﴾ in terms of meaning, and the implied form is: and We left in the story of Thamūd a sign; ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) for past time, attached to ﴿تركنا﴾; the clause ﴿قيل﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿تمتعوا﴾ is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying); ﴿حتى﴾ is a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive; ﴿حين﴾ is genitive (majrūr) by حتى; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿تمتعوا﴾.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t: ﴿فعتوا عن أمر ربهم فأخذتهم الصاعقة وهم ينظرون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction for sequence in the narration (al-tartīb al-ikhbārī); عتوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); عن أمر ربهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عتوا﴾; فأخذتهم الصاعقة is conjoined to عتوا; the wāw is circumstantial (of the ḥāl); هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ينظرون is the khabar (predicate); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:45-45.t: ﴿فما استطاعوا من قيام وما كانوا منتصرين﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; ما is negating; استطاعوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); من is a redundant (ṣila) preposition, and قيام is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw is conjunctive; ما is negating; كانوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw is its noun; and منتصرين is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:46-46.t: ﴿وقوم نوح من قبل إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; قوم is accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb understood implicitly, i.e.: and We destroyed the people of Nūḥ, and you may also take its implied form to be: and remember the people of Nūḥ; ومن قبل: من is a preposition, and قبل is an adverb (ẓarf), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun; the clause كانوا قومًا فاسقين is its khabar (predicate); and the clause of inna with what follows it has no grammatical position, because it gives the reason for their destruction.

muyesser-irab:47-47.t:
﴿والسماء بنيناها بأيد﴾: the wāw is resumptive. والسماء: accusative by al-ishtighāl (the verb being occupied with a pronoun of the noun), the implied form being: بنينا السماء بنيناها (We built the heaven; We built it). بنيناها: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause ﴿بنيناها﴾ is explicative, with no grammatical position. The clause بنينا السماء is conjoined to the preceding verbal clause. وبأيد: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of بنيناها, i.e. endowed with strength, or from its object, i.e. endowed with strength; or they are attached to ﴿بنيناها﴾, in which case the bāʾ is causal, i.e.: because of Our power. The clause ﴿والسماء بنيناها بأيد﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿وإنا لموسعون﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); موسعون is its khabar (predicate); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of بنيناها, or from its object.

muyesser-irab:48-48.t: ﴿والأرض فرشناها فنعم الماهدون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; والأرض: accusative by al-ishtighāl (the verb being occupied with a pronoun of the noun), the implied form being: فرشنا الأرض فرشناها (We spread the earth; We spread it); فرشناها: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿فرشناها﴾ is explicative, with no grammatical position; the fāʾ is conjunctive; نعم: an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise; الماهدون: the fāʿil of نعم; and the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, i.e.: نحن (We), and the clause is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:49-49.t: ﴿ومن كل شيء خلقنا زوجين لعلكم تذكرون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ومن كل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلقنا﴾, i.e.: We created of every thing two pairs; or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from زوجين, because it is originally a naʿt (adjective) of it, the implied form being: We created two pairs being of every thing; خلقنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); زوجين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لعل is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) expressing hope; ﴿كم﴾ is its noun; and the clause تذكرون is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:50-50.t:
﴿ففروا إلى الله﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause), and an omitted muḍāf must be implied, i.e.: to His reward; فروا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); وإلى الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فروا﴾.
﴿إني لكم منه نذير مبين﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its noun; ولكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نذير﴾, and منه is likewise attached; you may also attach it to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from نذير, because it is originally a naʿt (adjective) of it; نذير is the khabar (predicate) of إني; and مبين is a naʿt of نذير.

muyesser-irab:51-51.t:
﴿ولا تجعلوا مع الله إلها آخر﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; لا is the prohibitive lā; تجعلوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); مع الله is an adverb (ẓarf) of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted standing in the place of the second object; إلهًا: the first object (mafʿūl) of تجعلوا; and آخر is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿إلهًا﴾.
﴿إني لكم منه نذير مبين﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its noun; ولكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نذير﴾, and منه is likewise attached; you may also attach it to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from نذير, because it is originally a naʿt of it; نذير is the khabar (predicate) of إني; and مبين is a naʿt of نذير. This clause is repeated for emphasis: the first is tied to the abandonment of faith and obedience, and the second is tied to associating partners (al-ishrāk).

muyesser-irab:52-52.t:
﴿كذلك ما أتى الذين من قبلهم﴾: كذلك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: the matter and the affair (is like that). ما is negating. أتى is a past verb. الذين is its fronted object (mafʿūl). ومن قبلهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position.
﴿من رسول﴾: من: a redundant (ṣila) preposition. رسول is genitive by من in form and nominative in position, because it is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿إلا قالوا ساحر أو مجنون﴾: إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil. ساحر is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: أنت (you are); أو is a conjunction; and مجنون is conjoined to ساحر; the meaning of the conjunction has been discussed before. The clause إلا قالوا is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الذين من قبلهم, as if it were said: no messenger came to those before them except in the state of their saying: he is a sorcerer or a madman. The clause ﴿كذلك ما أتى...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:53-53.t: ﴿أتواصوا به بل هم قوم طاغون﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, rebuke and amazement; تواصوا is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), the wāw being the fāʿil of تواصوا; وبه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تواصوا﴾; بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); قوم is the khabar (predicate); and طاغون is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.

muyesser-irab:54-54.t: ﴿فتول عنهم فما أنت بملوم﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); فتول: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: أنت (you); وعنهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تول﴾; ﴿فما﴾: the fāʾ gives the reason for the command, and ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negating mā that operates like laysa; ﴿أنت﴾ is the noun of mā; ﴿بملوم﴾: the bāʾ is a redundant (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿ملوم﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative in position and genitive by the bāʾ in form.

muyesser-irab:55-55.t: ﴿وذكر فإن الذكرى تنفع المؤمنين﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ذكر is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: أنت (you); the fāʾ gives the reason for the command; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); الذكرى is its noun; and the clause تنفع المؤمنين is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:56-56.t: ﴿وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ما is negating; خلقت is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); الجن is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الإنس is conjoined to الجن; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); the lām is for causation (al-taʿlīl), or for consequence (al-ʿāqiba); يعبدون is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit أن after the lām of causation, and the sign of its accusative is the dropping of the nūn; the nūn that appears is the nūn of protection (al-wiqāya); the wāw is the fāʿil; the omitted first-person yāʾ is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi; and the lām of causation together with what it governs is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلقت﴾.

muyesser-irab:57-57.t: ﴿ما أريد منهم من رزق وما أريد أن يطعمون﴾: ما is negating; أريد is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: أنا (I); ومنهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أريد﴾; من is a redundant (ṣila) preposition, and رزق is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أريد﴾; the wāw is a conjunction, and ما أريد is conjoined to its counterpart; أن is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; ويطمعون [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the ayah is يطعمون] is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; the omitted first-person yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi; and أن with what falls in its scope is construed as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) serving as a mafʿūl bihi, i.e.: and I do not want their feeding Me.

muyesser-irab:58-58.t: ﴿إن الله هو الرزاق ذو القوة المتين﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the Name of Majesty is its noun; هو is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position; الرزاق is the first khabar (predicate) of inna; ذو القوة is a second khabar; and المتين is a third khabar; and it has been said: it is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الرزاق﴾ or of ﴿ذو﴾.

muyesser-irab:59-59.t: ﴿فإن للذين ظلموا ذنوبا مثل ذنوب أصحابهم فلا يستعجلون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); وللذين is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause ظلموا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ذنوبًا is the postponed noun of inna; مثل ذنوب أصحابهم is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ذنوبًا﴾; the fāʾ is conjunctive, ordering the prohibition of seeking to hasten; لا is the prohibitive lā; يستعجلون is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the sign of its jussive is the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the nūn that appears, with kasra, is for protection (al-wiqāya); and the omitted yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:60-60.t: ﴿فويل للذين كفروا من يومهم الذي يوعدون﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, ordering the establishment of woe for them; ويل is a mubtadaʾ (subject); it was permissible to begin with it because of the meaning of supplication it carries; وللذين is its khabar (predicate); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ومن يومهم is a naʿt (adjective) of ويل, and it has been said that it [Translator's note: i.e. من] has the meaning of «في» (in); الذي is a naʿt of يومهم; يوعدون is an imperfect verb, passive (built for the one whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and the clause يوعدون is the ṣila of الذي, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿والذاريات﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; الذاريات: genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of the oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم ("I swear").
﴿ذروًا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the governing word being the active participle; the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t: ﴿قتل الخراصون﴾: the clause is one of supplication (duʿāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; قتل: a passive past verb (built for an unnamed agent); الخراصون: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿الذين هم في غمرة ساهون﴾: الذين: an adjective of الخراصون; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); في غمرة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ساهون﴾; ساهون: the khabar (predicate) of ﴿هم﴾; the clause ﴿هم في غمرة ساهون﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause).

muyesser-irab:12-12.t: ﴿يسألون أيان يوم الدين﴾: يسألون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); أيان: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); يوم الدين: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is in the position of accusative as the object of يسألون.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿يوم هم على النار يفتنون﴾: يوم: a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being يقع ("it occurs") or يجيء ("it comes"); هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يفتنون is its khabar (predicate); على النار: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يفتنون﴾, على having the sense of في; the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the annexation of يوم to it.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿ذوقوا فتنتكم هذا الذي كنتم به تستعجلون﴾: the clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. "and it will be said to them at the time of the punishment: ذوقوا ('taste')". ذوقوا: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the tāʾ is its noun; به: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تستعجلون﴾; the clause تستعجلون is the khabar (predicate) of كان.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿إن المتقين في جنات وعيون﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); المتقين: its noun; في جنات: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of إن; عيون is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جنات.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿آخذين ما آتاهم ربهم﴾: آخذين: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun concealed (mustakinn) in the khabar (predicate) of إن, i.e. "they have settled, content with what He gave them and delighted with it"; ما: a relative noun in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of آخذين; the clause ﴿آتاهم ربهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿إنهم كانوا قبل ذلك محسنين﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿هم﴾: its noun; the clause ﴿كانوا﴾ is its khabar; the clause ﴿إنهم كانوا﴾ gives the reason for what was mentioned; قبل ذلك: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) محسنين; محسنين: the khabar of كانوا.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿كانوا﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the wāw of the group is its noun.
﴿قليلا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted adverb of time, i.e. "a little time"; or: standing in for an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "they used to sleep at night a little sleep".
﴿من الليل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of ﴿قليلا﴾.
﴿ما﴾: a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) particle.
﴿يهجعون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause يهجعون is the khabar (predicate) of كان. The clause ﴿كانوا قليلا من الليل ما يهجعون﴾ is in the position of nominative as a badal (substitute) from the clause ﴿كانوا قبل ذلك محسنين﴾, a badal of part from whole. Or it is an explicative clause, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿فالحاملات وقرا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction particle; الحاملات is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الذاريات; وقرًا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿فالجاريات﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction particle; الجاريات is also conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.
﴿يسرا﴾: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "with ease" or "made easy"; or: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) because it is an adjective of the maṣdar, i.e. "an easy running".

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿فالمقسمات أمرا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; المقسمات is also conjoined (maʿṭūf); أمرًا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿إنما توعدون لصادق﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the noun of ﴿إن﴾. The clause ﴿توعدون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position, and the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. توعدونه ("which you are promised"). The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). صادق: the khabar (predicate) of إن. Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the interpreted maṣdar from the maṣdariyya ﴿ما﴾ with what follows it is in the position of accusative as the noun of ﴿إن﴾, i.e. "your being promised is true". The clause ﴿توعدون﴾ is the ṣila of the maṣdariyya ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿إنما توعدون لصادق﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to the oath.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وإن الدين لواقع﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن is for emphasis and the accusative; الدين: its noun, accusative (manṣūb); لواقع: the lām is the shifted lām (muzaḥlaqa), and واقع is the khabar (predicate) of إن; the clause إن الدين لواقع is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to إن ما توعدون لصادق.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t: ﴿والسماء ذات الحبك﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; السماء: genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of the oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم ("I swear"). ذات: a naʿt (adjective) of السماء. الحبك: muḍāf ilayhi. The clause of the oath is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿إنكم لفي قول مختلف﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿كم﴾: its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); في قول: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of إن; مختلف: a naʿt (adjective) of قول. The clause ﴿إنكم لفي قول مختلف﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to the oath.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿يؤفك عنه من أفك﴾: the pronoun refers to the Qurʾān or to the Messenger; يؤفك: a passive imperfect verb (built for an unnamed agent); عنه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يؤفك﴾; من: a relative noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); أفك: a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "he"; the clause ﴿أُفِكَ﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause ﴿يؤفك﴾ is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as a second naʿt (adjective) of قول.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: وَالذَّارِياتِ is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of the oath, and the wāw is a substitute for the bāʾ. ذَرْواً is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the implied form is "by the scattering winds" (والرّياح الذاريات). One says: ذرت الريح الشيء, when it scatters it, so it is ذارية; and أذرت, so it is مذريّة.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: فَالْحامِلاتِ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الذّاريات, and the implied form is "then the clouds bearing the rain". This explanation is soundly reported from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. It was said: الحاملات are the ships; and it was said: the winds, because they carry the clouds. وِقْراً: everything carried on the back is a وقر (load).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: فَالْجارِياتِ is conjoined, i.e. "then the ships that run". يُسْراً is a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar, i.e. "an easy running".

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: فَالْمُقَسِّماتِ is conjoined as well, i.e. "then the angels who distribute what they have been commanded, by command".

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: I.e. of the reckoning, the reward and the punishment. And this is the answer to the oath.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: Conjoined. Ibn Zayd said: «لواقع» means "will surely come to be".

nahhas-irab:7-8.t:
وَالسَّماءِ is genitive by the oath. It was said: the implied form is "and by the Lord of the heaven", and likewise for everything that preceded. ذاتِ الْحُبُكِ
 is a naʿt (adjective). Al-Akhfash said: the singular is حباك. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: حباك and حبيكة. The answer to the oath is إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي قَوْلٍ مُخْتَلِفٍ (8). Qatāda said: in the sense of "differing": among you are those who affirm the Qur'an and those who deny it. Ibn Zayd said: some of them say "This is magic", and some of them say
something else — a differing saying; so in which [of these] is the truth?
