nahhas-irab:9-9.t: Al-Ḥasan said: he is turned away from faith and the Qur'an who is turned away. It was said: he is turned away from the saying, i.e. because of it, since they used to meet a man when he wanted to believe and say to him: "Magic and soothsaying", so he is turned away from faith.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty, قُتِلَ الْخَرَّاصُونَ (10): he said:
He is saying: "Cursed be the doubters." Ibn Zayd said: they fabricate lies, saying: "A poet", "a sorcerer", "he has brought magic", "a soothsayer" and "soothsaying", and "tales of the ancients which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening"; so they fabricate lies.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: الَّذِينَ is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of الخراصين; and هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and ساهُونَ is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the ṣila (relative clause). Outside the Qur'an, the accusative ساهين as a ḥāl (circumstantial) is permissible. فِي غَمْرَةٍ, i.e. in the covering of falsehood and ignorance; from it: "so-and-so is غمر (inexperienced)", and "غمر water", which covers whoever enters it; and from it الغمرة. Ibn Zayd said: heedless of what Allah has sent down and of His command and His prohibition.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: From Ibn ʿAbbās: they say, "When is the Day of Reckoning?" Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read إيان with a kasra on the hamza, and it is a dialect form.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
The grammarians differed concerning the accusative of «يوم». Abū Isḥāq said: its position is accusative, and the meaning is "the recompense will occur on the day when they are tried over the Fire". The grammarians other than him say: يوم is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from His saying أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الدِّينِ, and they spoke about [why it has] the accusative [form]. Al-Farrāʾ said: because it is annexed to two things [i.e. a clause]; and he permitted the nominative in it according to its basic state. Someone else said: because it is a non-genuine annexation (iḍāfa ghayr maḥḍa). The school of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is that adverbs of time are not fully declinable (ghayr mutamakkina), so when [one of them] is annexed to something indeclinable or to a clause like this, it is made indeclinable on the fatḥa; and they both permitted "مضى يوم قام" (the day he stood passed). The grammarians and the scholars of rare words recited from Imruʾ al-Qays [in the ṭawīl metre]: 434-
ويوم عقرت للعذارى مطيتي
(And the day I slaughtered my riding camel for the maidens)
 with «يوم» in the accusative, while its position is nominative according to those who relate «ولا سيّما يوم» and genitive according to those who relate «ولا سيّما يوم». [Translator's note: the two quoted variants are printed identically in the source; the intended forms are presumably «ولا سيّما يومٌ» (nominative) and «ولا سيّما يومٍ» (genitive).] Abū Jaʿfar said: We do not know of anyone who gave it the nominative or the genitive [in this verse], though analogy requires permitting these two. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ (13) — he said: they are punished. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: it is from their saying "فتنت الذهب والفضة" when you burn gold and silver in order to test them and purify them. One of the later scholars said: since الفتنة in the language is testing, it does not leave its [basic] meaning, and the meaning according to it is sound; the implied form is "the day when they are tested over the Fire", and it is said [to them]: ما سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ [al-Muddaththir: 42].

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: الذين هم — Mujāhid, ʿIkrima and Qatāda said: i.e. "your punishment". هذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), because in this world they used to ask for the punishment to be hastened, in mockery and denial. [Translator's note: the opening words «الذين هم» are as printed; the gloss "your punishment" belongs to ذُوقُوا فِتْنَتَكُمْ at the start of this verse.]

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: I.e. those who feared Allah the Exalted, by abandoning disobedience to Him and performing obedience to Him, are in gardens and rivers. Thus is the God-fearing one (المتّقي) when [the word] is unrestricted; if he guards against theft but does not guard against fornication, he is not called "God-fearing" (متّق), but he is called "one guarding against theft"; and so it is with this whole category.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: آخِذِينَ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and outside the Qur'an its nominative is permissible as the khabar (predicate) of «إن». As for the meaning of ما آتاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ, there are two views on it: one of them is "in Paradise"; and the other is that they act in this world in obedience to Allah, glory be to Him, and according to what He has made obligatory upon them, so they hold fast to it without exceeding it, as is related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty: آخِذِينَ ما آتاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ — he said: the obligatory duties; and from him: إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَبْلَ ذلِكَ مُحْسِنِينَ — he said: before the obligatory duties were made obligatory upon them.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: «ما» may be redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, the meaning being "they used to sleep little", i.e. a little sleeping. And «ما» with the verb may be [an interpreted] maṣdar (verbal noun), with «ما» in the position of the nominative, and «قليلا» accusative as the khabar (predicate) of «كان», i.e. "their sleeping was little of the night". Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: If you make «ما» a noun, you make «قليلا» nominative. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: يهجعون means "they sleep".

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: A group interpreted it in the sense of "they pray", because prayer is a request for forgiveness; and some of them interpreted it as meaning that they pray from the beginning of the night and seek forgiveness at its end; and this was regarded as recommended because Allah, glory be to Him, praised them for it. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd said: السّحر is the last sixth of the night.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: حَقٌّ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). لِلسَّائِلِ وَالْمَحْرُومِ: Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned the views of a group of scholars on المحروم there. And al-Zuhrī Muḥammad ibn Muslim told us that he said: المحروم is the one who does not ask. Most of the Companions hold that he is the one deprived of livelihood (المحارف). This is not contradictory, because المحروم in the language is one who is denied a thing, so it encompasses everything that has been said about it.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: I.e. lessons and admonitions for those of certain faith, which point to their Creator and His oneness.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: وَفِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ: Ibn Zayd said: and in His creating you. He said: and in them too are signs: the tongue, the eye and speech; and the heart, in which is the intellect — does anyone know what the intellect is and what its nature is? In all of that are signs. أَفَلا تُبْصِرُونَ, i.e. will you not then reflect, and so infer the greatness of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and His power?

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
وَفِي السَّماءِ رِزْقُكُمْ: [رزقكم] is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The people of interpretation differed on the meaning of His saying رِزْقُكُمْ, and on what provision is: is it the lawful and the unlawful, or the lawful only? Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: وَفِي السَّماءِ رِزْقُكُمْ
i.e. the rain. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: the snow and every melting spring. Wāṣil al-Aḥdab interpreted that to mean: "and from Allah, who is in the heaven, the Owner of your provision". And a [group of] people said:
everything a person earns is called provision (رزق). Others said: one does not say "Allah, Majestic and Mighty, provided him with it" except for what is lawful, and they cited as proof for this in the Qur'an that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَأَنْفِقُوا مِنْ ما رَزَقْناكُمْ [al-Munāfiqūn: 10], and He only commands spending from what is lawful. The people of interpretation differed on وَما تُوعَدُونَ. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Paradise and the Fire. Someone else said: توعدون is from وعد, and وعد is only for good, so what you are promised is for good; as for evil, one says أوعد. Others said: it is from أوعد, because توعدون in Arabic may be from أوعد and from وعد. The best thing said about it is what Mujāhid said; he said: what you are promised of good and evil, because the verse is general, so nothing is singled out by it except with a decisive proof.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
فَوَ رَبِّ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ is genitive by the oath. إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ, i.e. "Our saying: وَفِي السَّماءِ رِزْقُكُمْ وَما تُوعَدُونَ (22) is surely true". لَحَقٌّ مِثْلَ ما أَنَّكُمْ تَنْطِقُونَ: «مثل» with the nominative is the reading of the Kufans and Ibn Abī Isḥāq, as a naʿt (adjective) of حق; the Medinans and Abū ʿAmr read مثل ما in the accusative. There are several views on its accusative, the soundest of which is what Sībawayh said: that it is indeclinable (mabnī) because it is annexed to something not fully declinable, so it was made indeclinable; and analogous to it is وَمِنْ خِزْيِ يَوْمِئِذٍ [Hūd: 66]. Al-Kisāʾī said: «مثل ما» is accusative by "cutting off" (al-qaṭʿ). Some of the Basrans said: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from an indefinite noun. Al-Farrāʾ permitted the implied form to be "true (حقّا) like…", and he permitted «مثل» to be accusative in the sense of "like the like of" (كمثل), then the kāf was omitted and it was made accusative; and he permitted "زيد مثلك" and "مثل من أنت?", making «مثل» accusative according to the meaning, in the sense of كمثل. It was then held against him on this basis that he would have to say "عبد الله الأسد شدّة" in the sense of "like the lion", and he refused that, claiming that he permitted it only with مثل because the kāf can take its place. He recited [in the wāfir metre]: 435-
وزعت بكالهراوة اعوجّي ... إذا ونت الرّكاب جرى وثابا
(I restrained [it] with one like a staff, an Aʿwajī [steed], which, when the mounts flag, runs leaping.)
 Abū Jaʿfar said: These are divergent views, except the view of Sībawayh. There is also a question in the verse, namely that it is said: it has combined «ما» and «إنّ», while their meaning is one. Abū Jaʿfar said: There are two answers to this from the Kufan grammarians. One of them is that since the two words differ, that is permissible, as he said [in the wāfir metre]: 436-
فما إن طبّنا جبن ولكن ... منايانا ودولة آخرينا
(It is not cowardice that is our habit, but our fated deaths and the turn of fortune of others.)
 so he combined «ما» and «إن» while their meaning is one. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: بَلْ إِنْ يَعِدُ الظَّالِمُونَ [Fāṭir: 40], in the sense of "the wrongdoers do not promise". The other answer is that the addition of «ما» conveys a meaning, because had «ما» not been brought in, the meaning would be "it is true, not a lie"; but when you bring ما, the meaning becomes "it is true, just as the human being is one who speaks", as you say: "Is your speaking true?" in the sense of "Is it true or a lie?"
And you say: "Is it true that you speak?", so it conveys another meaning.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: He did not say أضياف (guests, plural), because ضيف is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and its literal sense in Arabic is "the account of those of the guesting (ذوي ضيف)", like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82].

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: إِذْ دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ, i.e. when they entered. فَقالُوا سَلاماً is accusative as a maṣdar; and it may be accusative by the verb falling upon it [as its object]. What indicates the soundness of this answer is that Sufyān related from Ibn Abī Najīḥ from Mujāhid: فَقالُوا سَلاماً — he said: [i.e.] something right (سدادا). قالَ سَلامٌ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "peace be upon you"; and it may be nominative as the khabar of a mubtadaʾ, the mubtadaʾ being omitted, i.e. "my affair is peace". Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read قالَ سَلامٌ, and there are two implied readings for it: one of them is that سلام and سلم are in one sense, like حلّ and حلال; and the implied form may be "we are peace (سلم)". [Translator's note: the source prints Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī's reading with the same spelling as the standard text; from the discussion, their reading is سِلْمٌ.] قَوْمٌ مُنْكَرُونَ: with an implied mubtadaʾ. He found them strange beforehand only because he did not know the like of them among guests.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
فَراغَ إِلى أَهْلِهِ, i.e. he went back, and its literal sense is "he went back secretly". فَجاءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ: the implied form is:
"so he came to his guests [with it]", then the object was omitted.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: The fāʾ indicates that the second follows the first; and «ألا» is [a particle of] alerting.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: فَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً, i.e. he concealed that and kept it hidden. قالُوا لا تَخَفْ: the ḍamma was dropped because of the jussive, and the alif because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلامٍ عَلِيمٍ, i.e. who will be knowledgeable. The Kufans related that when عليم refers to the future, عالم is said; and likewise with its analogues: one says "he is not generous (كريم), but he will be generous (لكارم) tomorrow", and "he has not died (مات), but he will die (لمائت)". Even though this is said, the Qur'an has come with something else.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: فَأَقْبَلَتِ امْرَأَتُهُ فِي صَرَّةٍ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: he said: with a cry. Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn Zayd and Ibn Sābiṭ said the same. It was also said: «في صرّة» means in a group of women hurrying to look at the angels. فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَها: Mujāhid said: she struck her forehead in astonishment. وَقالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ: one of the scholars claimed that عجوز is [nominative] with an implied verb, i.e. "Will an old woman give birth?" Abū Jaʿfar said: This is an error, because the interrogative particle is not omitted. The implied form according to the view of Abū Isḥāq is: "she said: I am a barren old woman", i.e. so how shall I give birth?

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: قالُوا كَذلِكَ قالَ رَبُّكِ, i.e. as we have told you, and this is not from ourselves. إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْحَكِيمُ in His disposal [of affairs]; الْعَلِيمُ, i.e. [who knows] the welfare of His creatures, and what has been and what will be.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: Ibrāhīm said to his guests: "What is your business, O you (يا أيها)…", and يا was omitted, as one says "زيد أقبل" (Zayd, come). «أي» is a singular vocative (munādā mufrad), and it is a complete noun, and الْمُرْسَلُونَ is its naʿt (adjective). [Translator's note: the source prints «من نعمته», evidently a misprint for «من نعته» "its adjective".]

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: I.e. they had committed crimes through disbelief. One also says جرموا, except that أجرموا with the alif is more common.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: I.e. so that We may rain upon them.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: مُسَوَّمَةً: there are two views on its meaning. The people of interpretation hold that its meaning is "marked". Ibn ʿAbbās said: the stone would be white with a black spot on it, and the stone would be black with a white spot on it. The other view is that the meaning of مسومة is "sent forth", from "سوّمت الإبل" (I let the camels loose to graze). لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ, i.e. for those who transgress the command of Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: فَأَخْرَجْنا مَنْ كانَ فِيها مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (35): [the pronoun in فيها] is an allusion to the town, though there was no prior mention of it, because the meaning is known. It may also be an allusion to the group.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: Mujāhid said: Lūṭ ﷺ and his two daughters, and no one else.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: The view of al-Farrāʾ is that «في» is redundant (zāʾida), and the meaning is "and We left it as a sign"; and in his view analogous to it is لَقَدْ كانَ فِي يُوسُفَ وَإِخْوَتِهِ آياتٌ لِلسَّائِلِينَ [Yūsuf: 7]. This far-fetched interpretation is unnecessary. Abū Isḥāq said: [the meaning is] "and We left in the city of the people of Lūṭ, upon him be peace, a sign for those who fear".

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: وَفِي مُوسى, i.e. and in Mūsā there is a sign and a lesson. إِذْ أَرْسَلْناهُ إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ: with a clear proof, such that whoever sees it realises that it is from Allah, glory be to Him. Qatāda said: بسلطان مبين, i.e. with a clear excuse.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t:
فَتَوَلَّى: so he turned away from the remembrance of Allah and went back. بِرُكْنِهِ: there are two views on it. The people of interpretation said: the meaning is "with his people"; Mujāhid and Qatāda said that. Ibn Zayd said: with his group. The other view, related by al-Farrāʾ: (بركنه) means "with himself". He said: the literal meaning of ركنه in the language is "with his side by which he strengthens himself". وَقالَ ساحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ: with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). Abū ʿUbayda holds that «أو» is in the sense of the wāw. He said: This interpretation, according to the skilled grammarians, is an error and a reversal of the meanings, and it is unnecessary, for أو has its own meaning. Abū ʿUbayda recited from Jarīr [in the wāfir metre]: 437-
أثعلبة الفوارس أو رياحا ... عدلت بهم طهيّة والخشابا
(Is it Thaʿlaba of the horsemen, or Riyāḥ, that you have equated with Ṭuhayya and al-Khishāb?)
 And this too is to be construed in that [same] way.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t:
َخَذْناهُ وَجُنُودَهُ
[جنوده] is conjoined to the hāʾ. نَبَذْناهُمْ فِي الْيَمِ
i.e. so We cast them into the sea.
هُوَ مُلِيمٌ
The original form is مليم; the vowel of the yāʾ was transferred to the lām, by way of assimilation. [Translator's note: so printed; the original form of مُلِيم (from ألام) would be مُلْوِم, whose vowel was transferred to the lām.]

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: I.e. and in ʿĀd there is a sign. The meaning is "barren of it" (معقومه); therefore the hāʾ was omitted.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: ما تَذَرُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ أَتَتْ عَلَيْهِ: the wāw was dropped from تذر because it is in the sense of تدع; and it was dropped from يدع because its original form is يودع, and it fell between a yāʾ and a kasra, so it was dropped. إِلَّا جَعَلَتْهُ كَالرَّمِيمِ: al-Farrāʾ said: الرميم is vegetation when it has dried and been trampled. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the basic meaning of الرميم is the old, decayed bone, and it is also called رمّة.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: وَفِي ثَمُودَ, i.e. a sign. إِذْ قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَمَتَّعُوا حَتَّى حِينٍ: al-Farrāʾ claimed that الحين here is three days; he held this because it was said to them: "Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days."

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: فَعَتَوْا عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِمْ, i.e. they exceeded bounds and abandoned the command of their Lord. فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ: it is related from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah have mercy on him, that he read «فأخذتهم الصاعقة», and its chain of transmission is weak, because it is only known from the ḥadīth of al-Suddī. What shows you that الصاعقة is more fitting is His saying, Majestic and Mighty, وَيُرْسِلُ الصَّواعِقَ [al-Raʿd: 13], for this is the plural of صاعقة, whereas the plural of صعقة is صعقات and صعاق. [Translator's note: ʿUmar's reading is printed with the same spelling as the standard text; from the argument that follows, it is «الصَّعْقَة».] وَهُمْ يَنْظُرُونَ: it was said: the meaning is "they were waiting for that", because they were awaiting the punishment when their colours changed during the three days.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: فَمَا اسْتَطاعُوا مِنْ قِيامٍ, i.e. rising up against the punishment. Al-Farrāʾ said: مِنْ قِيامٍ, i.e. they could not stand up to it; and he permitted in [ordinary] speech "من إقامة", as though he interpreted it in the sense of "they were not able to stand up to it". He claimed that مِنْ قِيامٍ is like وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ نَباتاً [Nūḥ: 17]. وَما كانُوا مُنْتَصِرِينَ, i.e. they were not able to take [their due] from the one who punished them. Qatāda said on the meaning of وَما كانُوا مُنْتَصِرِينَ: they had no strength by which to protect themselves from the punishment.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t:
وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِنْ قَبْلُ is the reading of the people of Medina and ʿĀṣim. Abū ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «وقوم نوح» in the genitive, conjoined to وفي ثمود, and the meaning with the genitive is "and in the people of Nūḥ there is a sign and a lesson". The accusative [can be explained] from more than one angle. Al-Farrāʾ has two views on it, and after them a third, also from him. The two are that the implied form is "so the thunderbolt seized them, and seized the people of Nūḥ"; and the second implied form is "and We destroyed the people of Nūḥ"; and the third, which came after them, is that the implied form is "and remember the people of Nūḥ". Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw that Abū Isḥāq had brought out this third view of his, and in it is [this] from his words: "And this is not more hateful to me than the two answers"; and he [Abū Isḥāq] expresses surprise at this and says: by this statement he has indicated that the three answers are hateful to him. He said: In this verse there is a good fourth view: that وقوم نوح is conjoined to أَخَذْناهُ وَجُنُودَهُ فَنَبَذْناهُمْ فِي الْيَمِ
because its meaning is "so We drowned them, and We drowned the people of Nūḥ". As for the reading with the accusative, it is the clear one according to the grammarians, apart from those we have mentioned who read otherwise. Abū ʿUbayd argued for the accusative that before it, in the stories that were in the genitive, all of them contain an explanation of what befell them, such as وَفِي عادٍ إِذْ أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّيحَ الْعَقِيمَ, and this is not [found] with the people of Nūḥ; so this indicates that it is not conjoined to the genitive, because it differs from it. He said: So how could it be "and in the people of Nūḥ" without mentioning what befell them? Someone else also said: when the distance between the genitive noun and what follows it is great, the Arabs do not conjoin it to it, but make it accusative. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَأُتْبِعُوا فِي هذِهِ الدُّنْيا لَعْنَةً وَيَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ [Hūd: 60], and we know of no one who read it in the genitive. And He, Majestic and Mighty, said:
فَبَشَّرْناها بِإِسْحاقَ وَمِنْ وَراءِ إِسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ [Hūd: 71], and most of the readers put it in the nominative and did not conjoin it to what precedes it. A third argument was mentioned by Sībawayh, namely that conjoining to what is nearer is more fitting; he related: "خشنت بصدره وصدر زيد" (I was rough with his chest and the chest of Zayd), and that the genitive is more fitting because of its nearness. So likewise here: "so the thunderbolt seized them, and seized the people of Nūḥ" is nearer than referring it back to ثمود. إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَوْماً فاسِقِينَ: [فاسقين] is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم, i.e. departing from obedience.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: وَالسَّماءَ is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and We built the heaven". بَنَيْناها بِأَيْدٍ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: (بأيد) means "with strength".

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْناها: also by an implied [verb]. فَنِعْمَ الْماهِدُونَ is nominative by نعم. The meaning is "and how excellent are the spreaders — We", then [نحن] was omitted.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: وَمِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنا زَوْجَيْنِ: it was said: the implied form is "and of everything We created, We created pairs". Mujāhid said about the pairs: misery and happiness, guidance and misguidance, faith and disbelief. Ibn Zayd said: the two pairs are the male and the female. Al-Farrāʾ combined them and said: the pairs, among animals, are the male and the female, and among others the sweet and the sour and what resembles that. لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ, i.e. so that you may take heed and know that worship is fitting only for the One who created these things.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: فَفِرُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ, i.e. to obedience to Him and His mercy, away from disobedience to Him and His punishment. إِنِّي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ, i.e. one who warns whoever disobeys Him of His punishment.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: وَلا تَجْعَلُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ, i.e. another object of worship, since worship is fitting only for Him. إِنِّي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ, i.e. I warn whoever worships other than Him of His punishment. إِنِّي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ comes twice, and it is not repetition, because in the second He warns whoever worships other than Allah, Majestic and Mighty, while in the first [He warns] whoever does not flee to the obedience of Allah and His mercy; and this may apply to those who affirm [Allah's] oneness.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: The kāf may be in the position of the nominative, i.e. "the matter is thus"; and it may be in the position of the accusative, in the sense of "thus did those before Quraysh: no messenger came to them except that they said this to him".

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: أَتَواصَوْا بِهِ, i.e. did some of them enjoin this upon others? بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ طاغُونَ: the meaning is: they did not enjoin it upon one another; rather, they are a people who transgressed and overstepped, and so opposed the command of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and His prohibition.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ: Mujāhid said: i.e. turn away. The implied form is: turn away from them until Our command concerning them comes to you; then the command to fight them came to him. فَما أَنْتَ بِمَلُومٍ, i.e. no blame will attach to you from your Lord, Majestic and Mighty, for any shortcoming of yours in warning them, for you have warned them and conveyed [the message] to them.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: وَذَكِّرْ, i.e. admonish them. فَإِنَّ الذِّكْرى تَنْفَعُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: ينفع (masculine) is also permissible, because الذكرى and الذكر are one.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: It was said: what is meant here is the believers specifically. The holder of this view argued that it follows [the mention of] the believers, so it is more fitting that the pronoun should be adjacent to them. The meaning of this is related from Zayd ibn Aslam. He said: and this is the school of most of the ḥadīth scholars. Al-Qutabī said: it is specific; so this is that same view, except that its expression is not good. It was also said concerning the verse what is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: that worship (العبادة) here is submission and compliance, and there is no Muslim or disbeliever but that he is submissive to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, compliant with His command, willingly or unwillingly, in what He has made his natural condition of health and sickness, beauty and ugliness, straitness and ease.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: ما أُرِيدُ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ رِزْقٍ: «ما» is in the position of the accusative, and «من» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. وَما أُرِيدُ أَنْ يُطْعِمُونِ: the nūn was dropped as the sign of the accusative, and the yāʾ was dropped because the kasra indicates it, and it is the end of a verse, so the dropping is good.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ, i.e. the Provider of His creatures, who guarantees their sustenance. ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَتِينُ with the nominative is read by those whose reading constitutes a proof, as a naʿt (adjective) of الرزاق and of ذو القوة, or as a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, or with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a naʿt of the noun of «إنّ» according to [its] position. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: الْمَتِينُ means "the strong". Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَتِينُ in the genitive, as a naʿt of القوة. [Translator's note: the source prints the genitive reading with the same vowelling as the standard text; their reading is الْمَتِينِ.] Abū Ḥātim claimed that the genitive is by close proximity (jiwār). Abū Jaʿfar said: Proximity does not occur in the Qur'an nor in eloquent speech, and according to the leading grammarians it is an error on the part of those Arabs who said it. Rather, what is to be said about the reading of those who put it in the genitive is that [القوة] is a non-real feminine. The implied form in it according to Abū Isḥāq is "of firm capability (ذو الاقتدار المتين)", because الاقتدار and القوة are one; and according to someone else, in the sense of "of firm determination (ذو الإبرام المتين)".

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ذَنُوباً مِثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحابِهِمْ فَلا يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ (59). فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ذَنُوباً: [ذنوبا] is the noun of «إنّ». مِثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحابِهِمْ is a naʿt (adjective). فَلا يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ, i.e. [ask Me to hasten] it.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: [ويل] is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the accusative is also permissible, i.e. "Allah has bound them to woe". مِنْ يَوْمِهِمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ, i.e. [the day] on which they are threatened with the descent of the punishment ...

safi-cedvel:1-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is the wāw of the oath. (الذاريات) is genitive by the wāw, attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is أقسم ("I swear"). (ذروا) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its governing element being الذاريات. (الفاء) is a conjunction in the three places. (وقرا) is the direct object of the active participle الحاملات. (يسرا) is an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, so it is its adjective [Note: or it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "easily moving".]. (أمرا) is the direct object of the active participle المقسّمات. (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, the ism of انّ [Note: and it is then good to separate (انّ) and (ما) in the written form ... It is also possible for (ما) to be a maṣdar particle, in which case the interpreted maṣdar is the ism of انّ.], and the returning pronoun is omitted; the (الواو) in (توعدون) is the deputy agent. (اللام) is the lām of the oath, a substitute for the shifted lām, giving emphasis, in both places.
Clause: «(أقسم) بالذاريات ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
And the clause: «توعدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause: «إنّ ما توعدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath.
And the clause: «إنّ الدين لواقع ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.

* Morphology:
(الذاريات) is the plural of الذارية, the feminine of الذاري, an active participle from the triliteral ذرا يذرو, on the pattern فاعل. It underwent ʿilāl by substitution; its origin was الذارو, and the wāw was changed to yāʾ because what precedes it has a kasra.. It is also possible that the verb is ذرى يذري of the bāb of ضرب, in which case there is no ʿilāl.
(ذروا) is a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb ذرا يذرو, on the pattern فعل with fatḥa and then sukūn.
(الحاملات) is the plural of الحاملة, the feminine of الحامل, an active participle from the triliteral حمل, on the pattern فاعل.
(وقرا) is a noun meaning "load", i.e. what is carried; its pattern is فعل with kasra and then sukūn.
(المقسّمات) is the plural of المقسّمة, the feminine of المقسّم, an active participle from the quadriliteral (form II) قسّم, on the pattern مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(الدين) is a noun meaning "recompense"; its pattern is فعل with kasra and then sukūn.. See also verse (4) of Sūrat al-Fātiḥa.

safi-cedvel:7-9.t:
* I'rab:
(والسماء) is like والذاريات. (ذات) is an adjective of السماء, genitive. (اللام) is the lām of the oath. (في قول) is attached to the khabar of إنّ. (عنه) is attached to (يؤفك). (من) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, a deputy agent; and the deputy agent of the verb (أفك) is a latent pronoun (ḍamīr mustatir) that is the returning pronoun.
Clause: «(أقسم) بالسماء ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «إنّكم لفي قول ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath.
And the clause: «يؤفك عنه من أفك» is in the position of the genitive, a second adjective of قول [Note: This holds if the pronoun in (عنه) refers back to القول ... It may refer to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and then the clause is resumptive.].
And the clause: «أفك» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).

* Morphology:
(7) الحبك: the plural of حبيكة, which is the path; it is either a noun of a thing or a noun of an idea, i.e. the sensible path or the intelligible path.

safi-cedvel:10-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, an adjective of (الخرّاصون). (في غمرة) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم). (ساهون) is a second khabar, nominative. (أيّان) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative, an adverb of time attached to an omitted element, a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (يوم), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "when is the coming of the Day of Recompense?"..
And the clause: «قتل الخرّاصون» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive and invocatory (duʿāʾiyya).
And the clause: «هم في غمرة» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause: «يسألون ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from (الخرّاصون).
And the clause: «أيّان يوم الدين» is in the position of the accusative, the direct object of the verb of asking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative; and the clause is restricted by the preposition.
13- (يوم) is an accusative adverb of time attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is يأتي (or يجيء). (على النار) is attached to (يفتنون), which is taken to include the meaning "they are exposed", and the (الواو) in (يفتنون) is the deputy agent..
And the clause: «(يجيء) يوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «هم على النار يفتنون» is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «يفتنون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم). 14- (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هذا). (به) is attached to (تستعجلون).
And the clause: «ذوقوا ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of an implied saying.
And the clause: «هذا الذي ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.
And the clause: «كنتم به تستعجلون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «تستعجلون» is in the position of the accusative, the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(الخرّاصون) is the plural of الخرّاص, the intensive form of the active participle from the triliteral خرص, of the bāb of نصر and the bāb of ضرب, meaning "to lie"; its pattern is فعّال with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(ساهون) is the plural of ساه, an active participle from the triliteral سها يسهو. ساه underwent ʿilāl by deletion because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; its pattern is فاع, and the pattern of ساهون is فاعون.

* Rhetoric:
Implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): in His words, Exalted is He, «ذُوقُوا فِتْنَتَكُمْ».
Here the punishment is likened to food that is eaten; then the thing likened to (al-mushabbah bihi) is omitted, and one of its concomitants is borrowed for it, namely tasting.

safi-cedvel:15-19.t:
* I'rab:
(في جنّات) is attached to the khabar of إنّ. (آخذين) is a ḥāl from the pronoun of settledness (istiqrār) which is the khabar of إنّ. (ما) is a relative noun, the direct object of the active participle (آخذين), and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "what their Lord gave them". (قبل) is an accusative adverb attached to (محسنين)..
Clause: «إنّ المتّقين في جنّات» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «آتاهم ربّهم» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause: «إنّهم كانوا» has no grammatical position; it gives a reason (taʿlīliyya).
And the clause: «كانوا ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
17- 18- (قليلا) is an accusative mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) standing in for the adverb, so it is its adjective, attached to (يهجعون) [Note: or an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "little sleeping" ... It may be the khabar of (كان) if (ما) is parsed as a maṣdar particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is then either the agent of (قليلا) or a badal of the ism of كان.]. (من الليل) is attached to an adjective of (قليلا). (ما) is redundant, to stress fewness [Note: or a maṣdar particle ...].. (بالأسحار) is attached to (يستغفرون)..
And the clause: «كانوا (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption [Note: or a badal of the clause كانوا ... محسنين, in the position of the nominative.].
And the clause: «يهجعون ... » is in the position of the accusative, the khabar of the second كانوا.
And the clause: «هم يستغفرون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كانوا (the second).
And the clause: «يستغفرون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
19- (الواو) is a conjunction. (في أموالهم) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (حقّ). (للسائل) is attached to an adjective of (حقّ), or to (حقّ). And the clause: «في أموالهم حقّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كانوا (the second).

* Morphology:
(19) السائل: an active participle from the triliteral سأل, on the pattern فاعل.
(المحروم) is a passive participle from the triliteral حرم, on the pattern مفعول.

safi-cedvel:20-23.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (في الأرض) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (آيات). (للموقنين) is attached to an adjective of (آيات)..
Clause: «في الأرض آيات ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
21- (الواو) is a conjunction. (في أنفسكم) is attached to what (في الأرض) is attached to [Note: or to a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, indicated by the mentioned آيات]. (الهمزة) is for an interrogative of rebuke (istifhām inkārī). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (لا) is negative.
And the clause: «لا تبصرون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.:
"Were you heedless, so that you do not see?"
22- (الواو) is a conjunction in both places. (في السّماء) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (رزقكم). (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, conjoined to رزقكم, and the (الواو) in (توعدون) is the deputy agent, with the returning pronoun omitted.
And the clause: «في السماء رزقكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause في الأرض آيات.
And the clause: «توعدون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
23- (الفاء) is a conjunction. (الواو) is the wāw of the oath. (ربّ) is genitive by the wāw, attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is أقسم. (اللام) is the lām of the oath, giving emphasis; it is a substitute for the shifted lām. (مثل) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in حقّ, accusative [Note: and according to some it is indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative, an adjective of حقّ, because it is annexed to an indeclinable word.]. (ما) is an indefinite described noun in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi [Note: or it is redundant, in which case it is good to write it joined to مثل, i.e. مثلما ... and the interpreted maṣdar is the muḍāf ilayhi.].
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّكم تنطقون ... ) is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is هو, i.e. "it is your speaking".
And the clause: « (أقسم) بربّ السماء» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause في السماء رزقكم [Note: It may be resumptive.].
And the clause: «انّه لحقّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath.
And the clause: « (هو) أنّكم تنطقون» is in the position of the genitive, an adjective of (ما).
And the clause: «تنطقون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of أنّ.

* Benefits:
- Allah is the guarantor of provision..
It is related from al-Aṣmaʿī that he said: I came from the Great Mosque of Basra, and a Bedouin appeared on a young camel (the offspring of a camel) and said: "Who is the man?" I said: "From the Banū Aṣmaʿ." He said: "And where are you coming from?"
I said: "From a place where the words of Allah the Mighty and Majestic are recited." He said: "Recite to me." So I recited: والذاريات, and when I reached (وَفِي السَّماءِ رِزْقُكُمْ) he said: "Enough for you." He got up to his she-camel, slaughtered it and distributed it to all who came and went, then took his sword and his bow, broke them and departed. When I later made the pilgrimage with al-Rashīd and was performing the circumambulation, there was someone calling to me in a soft voice. I turned, and it was the Bedouin, thin and yellowed. He greeted me and asked me to recite the sūra. When I reached that verse he cried out and said: "We have found what our Lord promised us to be true." Then he said: "Is there anything beyond this?" So I recited: (فورب السماء والأرض إنه لحق), and he cried out and said: "Glory be to Allah! Who is it that angered the Majestic until He swore? They did not believe Him until He swore." He said it three times, and his soul departed with it.

safi-cedvel:24-30.t:
* I'rab:
(هل) is an interrogative particle. (المكرمين) is an adjective of ضيف [Note: it came in the singular form while having the sense of the plural, because it is originally a maṣdar in which singular, dual and plural are alike.]. (إذ) is an adverb of past time in the position of the accusative, attached to (حديث) [Note: or attached to المكرمين, if what is meant is that Ibrāhīm honoured them by serving them ... or it is a noun of time functioning as a direct object of an omitted verb whose implied form is اذكر ("mention").]. (عليه) is attached to (دخلوا). (سلاما) is an absolute object of an omitted verb. (سلام) is a nominative mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "peace be upon you". (قوم) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is أنتم or هؤلاء..
Clause: «آتاك حديث ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «دخلوا ... » is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «قالوا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause دخلوا.
And the clause: « (نسلّم) سلاما ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.
And the clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: « (عليكم) سلام» is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.
And the clause: « (أنتم) قوم» has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.
26- (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places. (إلى أهله) is attached to (راغ). (بعجل) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of جاء..
And the clause: «راغ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال.
And the clause: «جاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause راغ.
27- (الفاء) is a conjunction. (إليهم) is attached to (قرّبه). (ألا) is a particle of offering..
And the clause: «قرّبه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause جاء.
And the clause: «قال ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with (قد) implied. And the clause: «ألا تأكلون ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.
28- (الفاء) is a conjunction. (منهم) is attached to a ḥāl from خيفة. (خيفة) is an accusative direct object. (لا) is a prohibitive particle that puts the verb in the jussive. (الواو) is circumstantial. (بغلام) is attached to (بشّروه)..
And the clause: «أوجس..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied clause, i.e. "they did not step forward, so he sensed...".
And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «لا تخف ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.
And the clause: «بشّروه ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with قد implied [Note: or without implying قد.].
29- (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places. (في صرّة) is a ḥāl from امرأته. (عجوز) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is أنا.
And the clause: «أقبلت امرأته ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قالوا.
And the clause: «صكّت ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أقبلت.
And the clause: «قالت ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause صكّت (or أقبلت). And the clause: « (أنا) عجوز ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.
30- (كذلك) is attached to an omitted absolute object whose governing element is the following قال [Note: i.e. "Your Lord said a saying like that saying which we have told you of", in the sense that He decreed and judged.]. (هو) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ [Note: It may be borrowed for the position of the accusative, as emphasis of the attached pronoun, the ism of إنّ.]. And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «قال ربّك ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.. The object of قال is omitted; it is what كذلك is attached to.
And the clause: «إنّه هو الحكيم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, giving a reason.
And the clause: «هو الحكيم ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(صرّة) is a noun meaning a cry, an uproar, or a group.. It is taken from the triliteral (صرّ); its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa and then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- The interrogative of affirmation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī): in His words, Exalted is He, «هَلْ أَتاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْراهِيمَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ», an interrogative of affirmation, magnifying the importance of the account and alerting that it is not among what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ knew other than by way of revelation. It is like when you begin to tell someone of something marvellous and ask him whether he has heard it or not: it is as though you expect him to say "No" and ask you to tell it.
2- Omission: in His words, Exalted is He, «قالَ سَلامٌ قَوْمٌ مُنْكَرُونَ».
It was said: it means "peace be upon you", and he turned it to the nominative by inchoation, intending permanence, so that his greeting would be better than theirs, in a fuller measure of courtesy and honour. And it was said: سلام is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "my affair is «peace»", and «قوم» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; most hold that the implied form is "you are an unfamiliar people", and that he, peace be upon him, said it to them in order to get to know them, as you might say to someone you meet: "I do not know you", meaning "tell me who you are and describe yourself".
3- Mursal metaphor (al-majāz al-mursal): in His words, Exalted is He, «قالُوا لا تَخَفْ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلامٍ عَلِيمٍ».
Here the boy is called "knowing" with regard to what his affair will come to when he grows up.

* Benefits:
- The clause that occurs as a direct object..
In this verse occur His words, Exalted is He: فَقَرَّبَهُ إِلَيْهِمْ قالَ أَلا تَأْكُلُونَ. The clause (أَلا تَأْكُلُونَ) is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.
We shall set out below what relates to the clause occurring as an object:
This clause occurs in three categories:
1- The category of quotation (ḥikāya) or its synonym, as in His words, Exalted is He: قالَ: إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ.
2- What is a quoted saying that is implied: His words فَدَعا رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ (وَنادى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ وَكانَ فِي مَعْزِلٍ يا بُنَيَّ ارْكَبْ مَعَنا): these clauses are in the position of the accusative by agreement; then the Basrans said: the accusative is due to an implied "saying", and the Kufans said: due to the verb mentioned. The Basrans are supported by the explicit mention of the saying in (وَنادى نُوحٌ رَبَّهُ فَقالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ ابْنِي مِنْ أَهْلِي) and (نادى رَبَّهُ نِداءً خَفِيًّا قالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَهَنَ الْعَظْمُ مِنِّي).
3- The category of suspension (taʿlīq): this is the verb's being suspended from seeking its object, in form but not in position, as in His words, Exalted is He: فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَيُّها أَزْكى طَعاماً. Suspension is not restricted to the chapter of ظنّ but is particular to every verb of the heart, as in His words, Exalted is He: أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا ما بِصاحِبِهِمْ مِنْ جِنَّةٍ and يَسْئَلُونَ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الدِّينِ. Sometimes the clause takes the place of two objects, as in His words, Exalted is He: وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنا أَشَدُّ عَذاباً and لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصى.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) links the response to an implied condition. (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ in the position of the nominative, its khabar being (خطبكم). (أيّها) is an indefinite, specified vocative (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative. (المرسلون) is a badal of أيّ (or an explicative apposition to it), following it in the nominative in form..
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «ما خطبكم ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have been sent for some matter, then what is your business?"; and the implied clause is the content of what was said. And the clause: «أيّها المرسلون» has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.

safi-cedvel:32-34.t:
* I'rab:
The pronoun (نا) is the deputy agent of the verb أرسلنا. (إلى قوم) is attached to (أرسلنا)..
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «إنّا أرسلنا ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said. And the clause: «أرسلنا ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of إنّ. 33- (اللام) is for giving a reason. (نرسل) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām. (عليهم) is attached to (نرسل). (من طين) is attached to an adjective of (حجارة).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن نرسل ... ) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (أرسلنا). And the clause: «نرسل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن). 34- (مسوّمة) is a second adjective of حجارة [Note: It may be a ḥāl of حجارة, because it is described by the preposition and its noun.]. (عند) is an accusative adverb attached to (مسوّمة), and likewise (للمسرفين).

safi-cedvel:35-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is a conjunction in both places. (من) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, a direct object. (فيها) is attached to the khabar of كان. (من المؤمنين) is attached to a ḥāl from the ism of كان, the returning pronoun. (ما) is negative. (غير) is an accusative direct object. (من المسلمين) is attached to an adjective of (غير) [Note: There is an omitted muḍāf in the speech, i.e. "other than a household of Muslims".]. (الواو) is a conjunction. The second (فيها) is attached to (تركنا). (للذين) is attached to an adjective of (آية)..
Clause: «أخرجنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "so they set about what they were commanded, and We brought out whoever was in it..".
And the clause: «كان فيها ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun. And the clause: «ما وجدنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أخرجنا.
And the clause: «تركنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ما وجدنا..
And the clause: «يخافون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).

safi-cedvel:38-40.t:
* I'rab:
(في موسى) is attached to an omitted verb indicated by what is mentioned in the preceding verse, i.e. "We left a sign" [Note: by taking the wāw as resumptive ... It may be conjoined to (فيها) in the preceding verse, in which case the preposition and its noun are attached to the mentioned (تركنا)]. (إذ) is an adverb in the position of the accusative, attached to the implied verb تركنا [Note: or attached to an adjective of آية, i.e. "existing at the time of Our sending ... or attached to آية"]. (إلى فرعون) is attached to (أرسلناه). (بسلطان) is attached to a ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (أرسلناه).
Clause: « (تركنا) في موسى ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «أرسلناه ... » is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
39- (الفاء) is a conjunction. (بركنه) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of تولّى [Note: i.e. he turned away, relying on his troops, because troops are to a king like a support (rukn) for him]. (ساحر) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is هو. (أو) is a conjunction. And the clause: «تولّى ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause أرسلناه. And the clause: «قال ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause تولّى. And the clause: « (هو) ساحر ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said. 40- (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places, and (الواو) likewise [Note: It may be the wāw of accompaniment, with وجنوده a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).]. (جنوده) is conjoined to the pronoun in (أخذناه). (في اليمّ) is attached to (نبذناهم). (الواو) is circumstantial ...
And the clause: «أخذناه ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause تولّى. And the clause: «نبذناهم ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause أخذناه. And the clause: «هو مليم ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of the object in (أخذناه) or in (نبذناهم). Part Twenty-seven
The remainder of Sūrat al-Dhāriyāt
From verse 41 to verse 60

safi-cedvel:41-42.t:
* I'rab:
(وفي عاد إذ أرسلنا) is like وفي موسى إذ أرسلناه, in words and clauses [Note: in verse (38) of this sūra]. (عليهم) is attached to (أرسلنا). (ما) is negative. (شيء) is genitive in form and accusative in position, a direct object. (عليه) is attached to (أتت). (إلّا) is for restriction. (كالرميم) is in the place of the second object.
And the clause: «ما تذر ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from الريح. And the clause: «أتت عليه» is in the position of the accusative, by position, an adjective of شيء. And the clause: «جعلته ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of تذر [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a second direct object of (تذر), in the sense of "leave", which takes two objects].

* Rhetoric:
Derivative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tabaʿiyya): in His words, Exalted is He, «الرِّيحَ الْعَقِيمَ».
It was called barren because it destroyed them and cut off their last remnant; so their destruction and the cutting off of their remnant were likened to the barrenness of women and their not conceiving, because of the loss of offspring in it; then the thing likened to was applied to the thing likened, and العقيم was derived from it.

safi-cedvel:43-45.t:
* I'rab:
«وفي ثمود إذ قيل» is like وفي موسى إذ أرسلناه, in words and clauses [Note: in verse (38) of this sūra.]. (لهم) is attached to (قيل). (حتّى حين) is attached to (تمتّعوا) ...
And the clause: «تمتّعوا ... » is in the position of the nominative, a deputy agent [Note: because it is originally a clause that is the content of what was said]. 44- (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places. (عتوا) is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the (الواو) is the agent. (عن أمر) is attached to (عتوا), which is taken to include the meaning أعرضوا ("they turned away"). (الواو) is circumstantial.
And the clause: «عتوا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause قيل. And the clause: «أخذتهم الصاعقة ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause عتوا. And the clause: «هم ينظرون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. And the clause: «ينظرون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم). 45- (الفاء) is a conjunction. (ما) is negative. (قيام) is genitive in form and accusative in position, a direct object. (ما) is like the first ...
And the clause: «ما استطاعوا....» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause أخذتهم. And the clause: «كانوا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause أخذتهم.

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (قوم) is a direct object of an omitted verb whose implied form is أهلكنا [Note: or اذكر.]. (قبل) is a noun of adverbial use, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive, attached to the implied verb. Clause: « (أهلكنا) قوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. And the clause: «إنّهم كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it gives a reason. And the clause: «كانوا قوما ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:47-51.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (السماء) is a direct object of an omitted verb that is explained by what follows. (بأيد) is a ḥāl from the agent of بنيناها or from its object [Note: or attached to (بنيناها), the باء being causal]; it is genitive by an implied kasra on the omitted yāʾ, because of the tanwīn. (الواو) is circumstantial. (اللام) is the shifted lām, giving emphasis..
Clause: « (بنينا) السماء ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. And the clause: «بنيناها ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative. And the clause: «إنّا لموسعون ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl ...
48- (الواو) is a conjunction. (الأرض) is like السماء. (الفاء) is a conjunction, and the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, i.e. نحن ("We").
And the clause: « (فرشنا) الأرض» ... ) has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause (بنينا). And the clause: «فرشناها ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative. And the clause: «نعم الماهدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied clause (فرشنا). 49- (الواو) is a conjunction. (من كلّ) is attached to (خلقنا) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from زوجين, an adjective that has been fronted before the described noun]. (تذكّرون) is an imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs was dropped ...
And the clause: «خلقنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied clause (فرشنا). And the clause: «لعلّكم تذكّرون» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption. And the clause: «تذكّرون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of لعلّ. 50- (الفاء) links the response to an implied condition. (إلى الله) is attached to (فرّوا), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "to the reward of Allah". (لكم) is attached to (نذير). (منه) is attached to a ḥāl from نذير.
And the clause: «فرّوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to an implied condition ..., i.e. "if you have known the attributes of Allah mentioned, then flee to Him". And the clause: «انّي لكم منه نذير ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption. 51- (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is a prohibitive particle that puts the verb in the jussive. (مع) is an accusative adverb attached to an omitted second direct object. (إنّي لكم ... ) is like the first. And the clause: «لا تجعلوا ... » is conjoined to the clause فرّوا. And the clause: «إنّي لكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(48) الماهدون: the plural of الماهد, an active participle from the triliteral مهد; its pattern is فاعل.

* Benefits:
Ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb)..
In this verse occur His words, Exalted is He: وَالسَّماءَ بَنَيْناها بِأَيْدٍ. السماء is accusative by ishtighāl. We shall set out below what relates to this topic:
Ishtighāl is when something that is an object in meaning is fronted before a governing element that has put the pronoun of this object in the accusative, such as (دارك رأيتها, "your house, I saw it"), or has put in the accusative something connected with its pronoun, such as (دارك طرقت بابها, "your house, I knocked on its door") and (أخاك مررت به, "your brother, I passed by him"). Were it not that the governing element is occupied with putting the pronoun, or what is connected with it, in the accusative, it would have put the fronted noun itself in the accusative. So they imply for this accusative noun a governing element of the same form as the mentioned verb, or of its meaning if it is intransitive. Thus the governing element in the second example is an omitted (طرقت), and in the last example it is from the meaning of the mentioned verb and not from its form, because it is an intransitive verb, and its implied form is (جاوزت أخاك مررت به).
In the preceding examples it is also permissible to put the fronted noun in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the clause after it as its khabar, so you say: (دارك رأيتها), (دارك طرقت بابها), (أخوك مررت به).
a- The accusative of the noun that the verb is occupied away from is obligatory when it occurs after what is particular to verbs, such as particles of condition and of urging, and particles of interrogation other than the hamza. Between this noun and what precedes it an omitted verb is implied obligatorily, so that the particle remains attached to what it is particular to, such as: (إن محمدا لقيته فأكرمه), (هلا فقيرا أطعمته), (متى أخاك لقيته), (هل الكتاب قرأته). The governing element mentioned after it then serves as an explanation of the omitted one.
b- The accusative is preferred in three places:
1- When it comes before a verb indicating a request, such as (الفقير أكرمه).
2- After the interrogative hamza, because the verb usually follows it: such as (أجارك تؤذيه؟).
3- When it heads the answer to a question, in the accusative. For example someone asks you: "What do you eat?"
You say: (رغيفا آكله).

safi-cedvel:52-55.t:
* I'rab:
(كذلك) is attached to an omitted khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter (or the case) is thus". (ما) is negative. (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, a direct object. (من قبلهم) is attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of the relative noun. (رسول) is genitive in form and nominative in position, the agent of أتى. (إلّا) is for restriction. (ساحر) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is هو. (أو) is a conjunction ...
Clause: « (الأمر) كذلك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. And the clause: «ما أتى ... من رسول» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption. And the clause: «قالوا ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the relative noun. And the clause: « (هو) ساحر ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said. 53- (الهمزة) is for an interrogative of rebuke. (تواصوا) is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. (به) is attached to (تواصوا). (بل) is for a transitional turning-away (iḍrāb intiqālī)..
And the clause: «تواصوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. And the clause: «هم قوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. 54- 55- (الفاء) links the response to an implied condition. (عنهم) is attached to (تولّ). (الفاء) gives a reason. (ما) is negative, working like ليس. (ملوم) is genitive in form by the باء and accusative in position, the khabar of ما ... (الواو) is resumptive. (الفاء) gives a reason..
And the clause: «تولّ ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if they do not respond to you, then turn away from them". And the clause: «ما أنت بملوم» has no grammatical position; it gives a reason. And the clause: «ذكّر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: It is said that this verse abrogates the preceding verse, "turn away from them ...", being revealed some time after the revelation of the first verse]. And the clause: «إن الذكرى تنفع ... » has no grammatical position; it gives a reason. And the clause: «تنفع ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(53) تواصوا: it has ʿilāl by deletion. The alif, the lām (final radical) of the word, was deleted because it met the wāw of the plural while quiescent, and what precedes the wāw remained with fatḥa to indicate the omitted alif; its pattern is تفاعوا.

* Benefits:
- The clause that occurs as a khabar..
The clause that occurs as a khabar is among the clauses that have a grammatical position. It is a khabar for three things:
1- A khabar for the mubtadaʾ, its position being the nominative, such as: (الله يعلم الغيب, "Allah knows the unseen") or (العلم كنوزه ثمينة, "knowledge, its treasures are precious").
2- A khabar for (إن) or one of its sisters, its position also being the nominative, as in His words, Exalted is He, in the verse we are concerned with: وَذَكِّرْ فَإِنَّ الذِّكْرى تَنْفَعُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ, or (إن البحر ركوبه خطير, "the sea, riding it is dangerous").
3- A khabar for the defective verb (كان and its sisters) or (كاد and its sisters), its position being the accusative, such as His words, Exalted is He: فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ عَلى ما أَنْفَقَ فِيها and وَإِنْ كادُوا لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ.

safi-cedvel:56-58.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (ما) is negative. (إلّا) is for restriction. (اللام) is for giving a reason. (يعبدون) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām ... and the (النون) is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) before the first-person yāʾ, which was omitted to suit the verse-ending.
Clause: «ما خلقت ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. And the clause: «يعبدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن), and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يعبدون ... ) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (خلقت). 57- (ما) is negative. (منهم) is attached to (أريد). (رزق) is genitive in form and accusative in position, a direct object. (ما أريد) is like the first. (يطعمون) is like يعبدون, and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يطعمون) is in the position of the accusative, a direct object, its governing element being أريد. And the clause: «ما أريد (the first)» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption. And the clause: «ما أريد (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the first clause أريد. 58- (هو) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الرزاق.. and the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ]. (الرزاق) is the khabar of إنّ, nominative. (ذو) is a second khabar, nominative [Note: or an adjective of الرزاق]. (المتين) is a third khabar [Note: or an adjective of (ذو). Or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is هو, and the clause is resumptive, confirming the content of what preceded]. And the clause: «إنّ الله ... الرزاق» has no grammatical position; it gives a reason.

* Morphology:
(58) الرزّاق: an intensive form from the triliteral رزق; its pattern is فعّال with fatḥa on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn. (58) المتين: a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from (متن) of the bāb of كرم, meaning hard and strong; its pattern is فعيل.

safi-cedvel:59-60.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) links the response to an implied condition in both places. (للذين) is attached to the khabar of إنّ. (مثل) is an adjective of (ذنوبا), accusative. (لا) is prohibitive, and the (النون) in (يستعجلون) is the nūn of protection before the first-person yāʾ, which was omitted to suit the verse-ending..
Clause: «إنّ للذين ظلموا ذنوبا ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the earlier nations had a share of punishment, then those who did wrong among the disbelievers of Mecca have a share like theirs". And the clause: «ظلموا..» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). And the clause: «لا يستعجلون» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if I delay their punishment, then let them not hasten Me". 60- (الفاء) links the response to an implied condition. (ويل) is a nominative mubtadaʾ [Note: an indefinite noun that carries a sense of reproach, so beginning with it is valid]. (للذين) is attached to an omitted element, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ويل. (من يومهم) is attached to the maṣdar (ويل), and the wāw in (يوعدون) is the deputy agent.
And the clause: «ويل للذين ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the time of their punishment (or the day of their punishment) comes, then woe to them". And the clause: «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). And the clause: «يوعدون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).

* Morphology:
(ذنوب) is a noun meaning a bucket with a tail, or a grave; its pattern is فعول with fatḥa and then ḍamma.

* Rhetoric:
Explicit representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya al-taṣrīḥiyya): in His words, Exalted is He, «فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ذَنُوباً مِثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحابِهِمْ».
الذنوب: the large bucket. This is a representation, whose origin is in water-drawers dividing the water, so that this one has a bucket and that one has a bucket. He said:
لنا ذنوب ولكم ذنوب ... فإن أبيتم فلنا القليب
(We have a bucketful and you have a bucketful; if you refuse, then the well is ours.)
The meaning: those of the people of Mecca who wronged the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by denial have a share of Allah's punishment, like the share of their fellows and peers among the earlier generations.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {ذَرْواً}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) of emphasis, governed by its derivative, which is the active participle. The object is omitted for brevity, since there is nothing comparable to what it scatters here. Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamza assimilated the «تاء» of «الذاريات» into the «ذال» of «ذَرْواً».

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {وَقْراً}: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «بالحاملات». «الوِقْر» with kasra is the name for what is loaded, that is, carried. It was also read «وَقْراً» with fatḥa, on the basis of naming the object by the maṣdar. It is also permissible that it be a maṣdar in its own right, governed by the sense of the preceding verb, since «الحمل» and «الوقر» have one meaning, even if there is generality and specificity between them.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {يُسْراً}: It is permissible that it be a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the sense of what precedes it, that is, «جَرْياً يُسْراً» ("an easy course"), and that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "possessing ease" or "possessing facility", or that they themselves be made ease, for emphasis.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {أَمْراً}: It is permissible that it be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), which is the apparent sense, and that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "that which is commanded"; on this it needs the object of «المُقَسِّمات» to be omitted. It may be said: there is no purpose in implying it, as with «الذَّارِيات». Are these different things, so that the «واو» is used in its usual sense of joining distinct things? For «الذاريات» are the winds, «الحاملات» the ships, «الجاريات» the stars, and «المُقَسِّمات» the angels. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is also possible that the wind alone is meant, because it brings the clouds into being, carries them, steers them, and runs in the air with an easy course." I say: on this it would be a joining of attributes while the one meant is single, as in his saying:
4100 - يا لَهْفَ زَيَّابَةَ للحارثِ الصَّا ... بِحِ فالغانِمِ فالآيِبِ
(Alas for Zayyāba, for al-Ḥārith, the dawn-raider, then the one who takes booty, then the one who returns!)
and the saying of another:
4101 - إلى المَلِك القَرْمِ وابْنِ الهُمامِ ... ولَيْثِ الكتيبةِ في المُزْدَحَمْ
(To the noble king, son of the valiant, and lion of the squadron in the press of battle.)
This is an oath, whose answer is His saying: «إنما تُوْعدون».

semin-durr:5-5.t: And «ما» may be a noun (ism), with its returning pronoun omitted, that is, «تُوْعَدونه»; or it may be a maṣdar particle, in which case it has no returning pronoun according to the well-known view. In that case «تُوْعدون» may be derived from «الوَعْد» (promise) or from «الوعيد» (threat), for it can be said «أَوْعَدْتُه فهو يُوْعَد» and «وَعَدْتُه فهو يُوعَد» without difference; so the implied sense is: "Indeed your promise" or "Indeed your threat." There is no need for the saying of those who said that in His saying «لَصادِقٌ» the active participle stands in the place of the maṣdar, that is, «لصِدْقٌ» ("truth"); for the wording of the active participle is more emphatic, since the promise or the threat is made truthful for emphasis, even though the attribute properly belongs to the one who promises or threatens.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {ذَاتِ الحبك}: The majority read «الحُبُك» with two ḍammas, which are the tracks, such as the tracks of sand and water when the wind strikes it; and «حُبُك الشَّعْر» are the marks of its curling and waving. Zuhayr said:
4102 - مُكَلَِلٌ بأصولِ النجم تَنْسُجُه ... ريحُ حَريقٍ لضاحي مائِه حُبُكُ
(Crowned with the roots of the plants, a fierce wind weaves ripples on the exposed face of its water.)
«الحُبُك» is a plural; its singular may be «حَبيكة», like «طريقة» and «طُرُق», or «حِباك», like «حِمار» and «حُمُر». The rajaz poet said:
4103 - كأنَّما جَلَّلها الحُوَّاكُ ... طِنْفِسَةٌ في وَشْيِها حِباكُ
(As if the weavers had covered it with a carpet whose embroidery has woven patterns.)
The root of «الحَبْك» is making a thing firm and well-made, and from this a coat of mail is called «مَحْبوكة». It was also said: «الحَبْك» is tightening and securing. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4104 - قد غدا يَحْمِلُنِي في أَنْفِه ... لاحِقُ الإِطْلَيْنِ مَحْبوكٌ مُمَرّْ
(He set out carrying me on his nose-ridge: a horse lean in the flanks, tightly built, strongly twisted.)
There are many readings of this word. From al-Ḥasan there are six: «الحُبُك» with ḍamma as the majority; «الحُبْك» with ḍamma and sukūn, which is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū ʿAmr; «الحِبِك» with kasra on both; «الحِبْك» with kasra and sukūn, which is a lightening of the kasra form; «الحِبَك» with kasra and fatḥa; and «الحِبُك» with kasra and ḍamma. Of these six, the last is the most troubling, because this pattern is unused among Arabic forms. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others said: "It is from talfīq (mixing)", meaning that there are two dialects, kasra on the «حاء» and the «باء», and ḍamma on both; so this reader took the kasra from one dialect and the ḍamma from the other. People found this unlikely, since mixing only occurs between two words. The Shaykh explained it on the basis that the «حاء» was made to follow the vowel of the «تاء» in «ذات»; he said: "He did not count the «لام» as a separator, since it is sukūn, and so it is a weak barrier." Abū Mālik al-Ghifārī agreed with al-Ḥasan on this reading. ʿIkrima read it with ḍamma and fatḥa, as the plural of «حُبْكة», like «غُرْفة» and «غُرَف». Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Mālik read «الحَبَك» with two fatḥas, the plural of «حَبَكة», like «عَقَبة» and «عَقَب». These are eight readings.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {إِنَّكُمْ}: this is the answer to the oath.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ}: an adjective of «قول». The pronoun in «عنه» refers to the Qur'an, or to the Messenger, or to the religion, or to what you are promised, that is, "he is turned away from it". It was also said: «عن» is causal, and the thing turned away from is omitted; the pronoun in «عنه» on this refers to «قولٍ مختلفٍ», that is, "because of the saying, whoever wants Islam is turned away, by someone saying: it is magic, it is soothsaying." The majority read both verbs in the passive. Qatāda and Ibn Jubayr read «يُؤْفَكُ عنه مَنْ أَفَك», the first passive and the second active, that is, "he is turned away from it who turned people away from it." Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يَأْفَكُ» in the active, from «أفك الشيء», that is, "he turns people away from it who is himself turned away." From him also: «يَأْفِكُ عنه مَنْ أَفَّك» with shadda, that is, "who is himself a great liar." It was also read «يُؤْفَنُ عنه مَنْ أُفِنَ» with «نون» in both, that is, "he is deprived of it who is deprived", from «أَفِنَ الضَّرْعَ» when one exhausts it by milking.

semin-durr:10-10.t: It was also read «قَتَل» in the active, the subject being Allah the Exalted, with «الخَرَّاصين» as its object.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الدين}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). It was said: both are adverbials, so how can one adverbial occur within another? The reply: it is on the basis of an omitted event, that is, "when is the occurrence of the day", so «أيَّان» is an adverbial for the occurrence. The reading «إيَّان» with kasra was mentioned in al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ هُمْ}: It is permissible that it be accusative by an implied element, that is, "the recompense will come on the day when they...". It is also permissible that it be a badal (substitute) from «يومُ الدين», the fatḥa being a fatḥa of indeclinability (binā') according to the view of those who allow the adverbial to be indeclinable even when annexed to a nominal clause. On this it would be a report of the meaning of their words, spoken in mockery; had it come as a report of their earlier wording, it would have been said: «يومَ نحن على النار نُفْتَنُ». And «يوم» is accusative by «الدين». It was also said: by an implied verb, that is, «يَحارون» ("they will be bewildered"). It was also said: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied «أعني» ("I mean"). «يُفْتَنون» is made transitive by «على» because it has the sense of "being tested". It was also said: «على» has the sense of «في». It was also said that «يومَ هم» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, «هو يومَ هم», with the fatḥa for the reason given. This is supported by the reading of Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Zaʿfarānī, «يومُ هم» with nominative, and it likewise supports the view of badal. A similar matter was discussed in Ghāfir.

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying: {ذُوقُواْ}: that is, "it is said to them: Taste." And «هذا الذي كنتم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); this is the apparent sense. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that «هذا» be a badal (substitute) from «فِتْنتكم», because it has the sense of punishment.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {آخِذِينَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in His saying «جناتٍ». And «ما آتاهم» means from what is in Paradise, so it is a true ḥāl. It was also said: what He gave them of His commands and prohibitions in this world, in which case it is a reported ḥāl, because of the difference of the two times. He made the prepositional phrase here the khabar (predicate) and the adjective an addition, and reversed this in His saying {إِنَّ المجرمين فِي عَذَابِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدُونَ} [الزخرف: 74]. It was said: because the khabar is the point of the sentence. The aim there is to report their eternal stay, because the believer may enter the Fire, but he must come out of it. As for the verse of the God-fearing, He made the adverbial the khabar for their security of not leaving it, making that the focus of the benefit so that they obtain reassurance; so the adjective became accusative as a ḥāl.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {كَانُواْ قَلِيلاً}: There are several views. The first: that the sentence is complete at «قليلاً»; for this reason some paused at «قليلاً» to match His saying {وَقَلِيلٌ مَّا هُمْ} [ص: 24] and {وَقَلِيلٌ مِّنْ عِبَادِيَ الشكور} [سبأ: 13], and began {مِّن الليل مَا يَهْجَعُونَ}, that is, "what they sleep of the night." This is not clear in meaning or in grammar. As to the first, they must sleep, and a negation of their sleeping cannot be conceived. As to grammar, what lies within the scope of a negation does not precede it according to the Basrans; this is if you take «ما» as negative; and if you take it as a maṣdar (verbal noun) particle, the implied sense becomes "of the night is their sleeping", which has no benefit, since all other people are the same.
