The second: that «ما» is a maṣdar particle in the position of nominative by «قليلاً». The implied sense: "their sleeping was little".
The third: that the maṣdar «ما» is a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from the ism of kāna, that is, "their sleeping was little"; and «من الليل» on these two views is not attached to «يَهْجَعون», because what lies in the scope of the maṣdar does not precede it according to the well-known view; some of those who forbid it excuse it in the case of an adverbial, so it is allowed according to them, while the forbidder implies a verb indicated by «يَهْجَعون», that is, "they slept of the night".
The fourth: that «ما» is redundant and «يَهْجَعون» is the khabar of kāna. The implied sense: "they slept of the night a little sleep," or "a little time"; so «قليلاً» is an adjective of a maṣdar or of an adverbial.
The fifth: that it has the sense of «الذي», with its returning pronoun omitted, the implied sense being: "they were a little of the night, the time in which they sleep"; and this involves strain.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {وبالأسحار}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَسْتَغْفرون». The «باء» has the sense of «في». What is attached to the khabar (predicate) is put before the mubtadaʾ (subject), since it is permissible to bring the governing element forward.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {وفي أَنفُسِكُمْ}: a conjunction (nasaq) on «في الأرض», so it is also a khabar (predicate) for «آياتٌ». The implied sense: "in the earth and in yourselves are signs." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Whoever makes it nominative by the adverbial makes the pronoun of the signs be in the adverbial." He means whoever makes the agent nominative by the adverbial absolutely, that is, even if it does not rest on something before it, makes this preposition raise an agent which is the pronoun of «آياتٌ». Some allowed that it be attached to «تُبْصِرُون», but this is invalid, because the interrogative and the «فاء» prevent it. Qatāda read «آيَةٌ» [الذاريات: 20] in the singular.

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying {رِزْقُكُمْ}: that is, "the cause of your provision". Ḥumayd and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «رازِقُكم», an active participle; and Allah the Exalted is far above direction.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
The pronoun in «إنَّه لحقٌّ» is either for the Qur'an, or for the religion, or for the day in His saying {وَإِنَّ الدين لَوَاقِعٌ} [الذاريات: 6], {يَوْمَ هُم} [الذاريات: 13], {يَوْمُ الدين} [الذاريات: 12], or for the Prophet ﷺ.
His saying {مِثْلَ مَا}: the two (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Abū Bakr read «مثلُ» with nominative, and there are three views on it. The first: that it is a second, independent khabar (predicate), like the first. The second: that it, together with what precedes it, forms a single khabar, as in «هذا حُلْوٌ حامِضٌ» ("this is sweet-sour"); Abū al-Baqāʾ reported these two. The third: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «حق»; and «ما» is redundant on all three views. «أنَّكم» is the muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), that is, «لَحَقٌّ مثلُ نُطْقِكم» ("a truth like your speaking"). It does no harm to imply its annexation to a definite word, because it does not become definite by that, owing to its vagueness.
The rest read it with accusative, and there are several views on it. The best known: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «حَقٌّ» as in the first reading, and the noun was made indeclinable because of its annexation to something not fully inflected, as the other poet made it indeclinable in his saying:
4105 - فتَداعَى مَنْخِراه بدَمٍ ... مثلَ ما أثمرَ حَمَّاضُ الجَبَلْ
(His two nostrils called to each other with blood, like what the sorrel of the mountain bears as fruit.)
with fatḥa on «مثلَ» though it is a naʿt of «دم»; and as «غيرَ» was made indeclinable in his saying:
4106 - لم يَمْنَعِ الشُّرْبَ منها غيرَ أَن نَطَقَتْ ... حمامةٌ في غُصونٍ ذاتِ أَوْقالِ
(Nothing prevented the drinking from it except that a dove cooed in branches full of foliage.)
where «غيرَ» is the fāʿil (agent) of «يَمْنع» and he made it indeclinable on fatḥa because of its annexation to «أنْ نَطَقَتْ». What was said earlier on the reading with fatḥa of {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ} [الأنعام: 94] spares me from restating this.
The second: that «مثلَ» was compounded with «ما» until the two became one thing. Al-Māzinī said: "Like it are «وَيْحَما», «هَيَّما» and «أَيْنَما»", and he quoted Ḥumayd ibn Thawr:
4107 - ألا هَيَّما مِمَّا لَقِيْتُ وهَيَّما ... ووَيْحاً لِمَنْ لم يَدْرِ ما هُنَّ وَيْحَما
(Ah, such longing from what I have met, such longing! And woe to him who did not know what they are, woe!)
He said: were it not for indeclinability, it would be with tanwīn. He also quoted:
4108 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فأكْرِمْ بنا أُمَّاً وأكْرِمْ بنا ابْنَما
(... How noble through us is a mother, and how noble through us is a son!)
Some grammarians held what he mentioned, and quoted:
4109 - أثورَ ما أَصِيْدُكم أم ثورَيْنْ ... أم هذه الجَمَّاءَ ذاتَ القرنَيْنْ
(Shall I hunt for you a bull, or two bulls, or this hornless one that has two horns?)
But as for his quotation of «وأكرِمْ بنا ابنَما», this does not belong to the topic, because this is «ابن» to which a «ميم» has been added; and when a «ميم» is added to it, the «نون» is made to follow the «ميم» in vowels according to the eloquent usage, so you say «هذا ابنمٌ», «ورأيت ابنَماً», «ومررت بابنِم», with the case vowels falling on the «ميم» and the «نون» following. And «ابنما» in the verse is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), so the fatḥa is due to the accusative, not to indeclinability; and this is not the redundant «ما», rather the «ميم» alone is redundant and the «ألف» is a replacement for tanwīn.
The third: that it is accusative as an adverbial; this is the view of the Kufans, who allow «زيدٌ مثلَك» with fatḥa. Abū al-Baqāʾ reported it from Abū al-Ḥasan, but in a problematic wording; he said: "It is read with fatḥa, and there are two views on it: one, it is inflected, and then there are several views on its accusative." Then he said: "Or that it is nominative in position but was given fatḥa as the adverbial was given fatḥa in His saying {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ} [الأنعام: 94] according to al-Akhfash." Then he said: "And the second view is that it is indeclinable." Abū ʿUbayd said: "Some Arabs always make «مثل» accusative, saying: «هذا رجلٌ مثلَك»."
The fourth: that it is accusative by dropping the preposition, which is the «كاف» of comparison. Al-Farrāʾ said: "The Arabs make it accusative when a noun, meaning the mubtadaʾ, is raised by it, saying: «مثلَ مَنْ عبدُ الله؟», «وعبدُ الله مثلَك», «وأنت مثلَه»; because the «كاف» may enter upon it, so it is made accusative when you drop the «كاف»." I say: there is room for objection in this. What need is there to imply the entering of the «كاف» when «مثل» gives its benefit? It is as if he saw the «كاف» entering upon it in His saying {لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ} [الشورى: 11] and said that.
The fifth: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, that is, «لَحَقٌّ حقاً مثلَ نُطْقِكم». The sixth: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «لَحَقٌّ», because qualifying with this maṣdar has become so frequent that it runs in the course of derived attributes, and the operator on it is «حَقٌّ». The seventh: that it is a ḥāl from «حقٌّ» itself, even though it is indefinite. Sībawayh stated its permissibility in several places in his book, and Abū ʿUmar followed him in that.
This «ما», in a construction like this, as in their saying «هذا حَقٌّ كما أنَّك ههنا» ("this is as true as that you are here"), may not be dropped, so it is not said «هذا حَقٌّ كأنَّك هنا». Al-Khalīl, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, stated this. When you make «مثل» inflected, «ما» is redundant and «أنكم» is in the position of genitive by annexation, as mentioned; and when you make it indeclinable, either by compounding or by its annexation to something not fully inflected, two views are allowed for this «ما»: that it is redundant, and that it is an indefinite noun with an adjective; so said Abū al-Baqāʾ. There is room for objection in it, because of the absence of an adjective here. If he says: it is omitted, then the default is non-omission. Moreover, they have stated that this adjective is not omitted because its qualified noun is vague. As for «أنَّكم تَنْطِقون», it may be genitive by annexation if «ما» is redundant; and if it is indefinite, it is in the position of accusative by an implied «أعني», or nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {إِذْ دَخَلُواْ}: There are four views on what governs «إذ». The first: that it is «حديثُ», that is, "has the account of them reached you, occurring at the time of their entering upon him?" The second: that it is accusative by the sense of the verb in «ضَيْف», because originally it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and for this reason the masculine singular and others are alike in it, as if it were said: "those whom he entertained at the time of their entering upon him". The third: that it is accusative by «المُكْرَمين», if by their being honoured is meant that Ibrāhīm honoured them by serving them. The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied «اذْكُر» ("remember"); and it is not permissible to make it accusative by «أتاك», because of the difference of the two times.
The majority read «المُكْرَمين» with the «راء» light, from «أكرم»; ʿIkrima read it with shadda.
His saying: {سَلاَماً قَالَ سَلاَمٌ}: its treatment was given earlier in Hūd. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is plausible that «قالوا» governs «سَلاماً», making «سلاماً» in the sense of «قولاً», and the meaning then is: they said a greeting and a saying whose meaning is 'peace'. This is the view of Mujāhid." I say: it would be better to make the implied sense that they said this very wording, and the explanation of this wording is the customary greeting. The differences of the readers over «سلاماً», regarding fatḥa or kasra of its «سين» and sukūn or fatḥa of its «لام», were also mentioned earlier.
The majority read the first «سلاماً» accusative and the second nominative; they were also read both nominative; and it was read «سَلاماً قال: سِلْماً» with kasra on the «سين» of the second and accusative. The justification of all this is not hidden, from what was said in Hūd.
His saying: {قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ}: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); they implied: «أنتم قومٌ». Some did not find this good, because it lacks friendliness, and the like of it would not occur from Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him; so it is better to imply «هؤلاء قومٌ» or «هم قومٌ», and this saying of his would be to the people of his household and his close ones, not to the guest himself, because that would alarm them.

semin-durr:26-26.t: And His saying: {فَجَآءَ}: a conjunction on «فراغَ», and its being caused by it is clear. The hamza in «ألا تأكلون» is for reproach of them for not eating, or an offer, or an urging.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {فِي صَرَّةٍ}: It is permissible that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent), that is, "being in a cry". «الصَّرَّة» was said to be the shout. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4110 - فَأَلْحَقَنا بالهادياتِ ودونَه ... جَواحِرُها في صَرَّةٍ لم تَزَيَّلِ
(He brought us up with the leaders, and before him the hounds in a throng that did not disperse.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is from «صَرَّ الجُنْدُبُ» (the locust chirped), «والبابُ» (the door creaked) and «والقلمُ» (the pen scratched). Its position is accusative as a ḥāl, that is, «فجاءَتْ صارَّةً» (she came crying out)." It is also permissible that it be attached to «أَقْبَلَتْ», that is, "she came forward among a group of women who were with her." «الصَّرَّةُ» is a group of women.
His saying: {فَصَكَّتْ}: that is, she slapped. There was disagreement about it. It was said: it is striking with the hand outstretched. It was also said: rather, it is striking the face with the fingertips, as one does in amazement, and this is the custom of women.
His saying «عجوزٌ»: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, «أنا عجوزٌ عقيمٌ فكيف أَلِدُ؟» ("I am an old barren woman, so how can I give birth?"). The other verse explains it.

semin-durr:30-30.t: His saying: {كَذَلِكَ}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) governed by the second «قال», that is, "just as the saying we have told you, your Lord has said", meaning that it is from Allah, so do not be amazed at it.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {مُّسَوَّمَةً}: There are three views. The first: that it is accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «حجارة». The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in the preposition phrase before it. The third: that it is a ḥāl from «حجارة», and what made this good is that the indefinite noun was qualified by the prepositional phrase after it.
His saying: {عِندَ رَبِّكَ}: an adverbial for «مُسَوَّمةً», that is, "marked with Him".

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {فِيهَآ آيَةً}: It is permissible that the pronoun refer to the town, that is, "we left in the town a sign, such as the stones or the foul water"; and it is permissible that it refer to the destruction understood from the context.

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {وَفِي موسى}: There are several views. The first, which is the apparent one: that it is a conjunction on His saying «فيها» with repetition of the preposition, because what is conjoined to is a genitive pronoun; so it is attached to «تَرَكْنا» in meaning, and the implied sense is: "and we left in the story of Mūsā a sign." This is a clear meaning. The second: that it is conjoined to His saying {وَفِي الأرض آيَاتٌ} [الذاريات: 20], that is, "in the earth and in Mūsā are signs for those who are certain"; al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The Shaykh said: "This is very far-fetched; the Qur'an is to be kept above the like of it." I say: the reason he finds it far-fetched is the distance between them, though the people of knowledge have done this in cases of greater distance. The third: that it is attached to an implied «جَعَلْنا», indicated by «وتَرَكْنا». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or on His saying", meaning it may be conjoined to «وتَرَكْنا فيها آيةً» in the sense of: "and we made in Mūsā a sign", as in his saying:
4111 - فَعَلَفْتُها تِبْناً وماءً بارداً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I fed her straw and cold water ...)
The Shaykh said: "There is no need to imply «وجَعَلْنا», for it is possible that the governor of the prepositional phrase be «وتَرَكْنا»." I say: al-Zamakhsharī meant only the first view, as the evidence of his saying: "«وفي موسى» is conjoined to «وفي الأرض» or to his saying «وتركْنا فيها»." He said "in the sense of" only from the side of explaining the meaning, not the grammar, and he made the verb overt only to point out that the two verbs differ. He means that this leaving is other than that leaving, and for that reason he brought it out with the root «الجَعْل» rather than the root «الترك», so that the difference would show.
His saying: {إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَاهُ}: Three views are permissible for this adverbial. The first: that it is accusative by «آية» on the first view, that is, "we left in the story of Mūsā a sign at the time of our sending him". The second: that it is attached to an omitted element because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «آية», that is, "a sign existing at the time of our sending". The third: that it is accusative by «تَرَكْنا».
His saying: {بِسُلْطَانٍ}: It is permissible that it be attached to the sending itself, and that it be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, either from Mūsā or from his pronoun, that is, "coupled with authority", which is the proof.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {بِرُكْنِهِ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تَوَلَّى».
His saying: {سَاحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ}: «أو» here is in its usual sense of vagueness for the listener, or of doubt; he put himself, although he knew him to be a true prophet, in the position of one in doubt about his affair, to deceive his people. Abū ʿUbayda said: "«أو» has the sense of «و»." He said: "because he said both; Allah the Exalted said {إِنَّ هذا لَسَاحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ} [الأعراف: 109], and in another place {إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ الذي أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ} [الشعراء: 27]. And «أو» comes with the sense of «و», as in his saying:
4112 - أثَعْلَبَةَ الفوارِسَ أو رِياحا ... عَدَلْتَ بهم طُهَيَّةَ والخِشابا
(Did you set Ṭuhayya and al-Khishāb equal to Thaʿlaba the horsemen, or Riyāḥ?)"
People rejected this from him and said: no necessity calls for that; and as for the two verses, they do not indicate that he said both together, but only that he said both, which is more general than their being together, this at one time and that at another.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {وَجُنُودَهُ}: It is permissible that it be conjoined to the object of «أَخَذْناه», which is the apparent sense, and that it be a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).
His saying: {وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause. If it is a ḥāl from the object of «نَبَذْناهم», then the «واو» is necessary, since it contains no mention returning to the owner of the ḥāl; and if it is a ḥāl from the object of «أَخَذْناه», the «واو» is not obligatory, since the clause has a mention returning to it. It may be said: the pronoun in «نَبَذْناهم» refers to Pharaoh and his troops, so the ḥāl comes to have a mention returning to part of what the first pronoun included. There is room for objection in this, since it becomes like your saying: «جاء السلطانُ وجنوده فأكرمتُهم راكباً فرسَه» ("the sultan and his troops came, and I honoured them, riding his horse"), where you make «راكباً» a ḥāl from part of what the pronoun of «أكرمتُهم» included.

semin-durr:41-41.t: His saying: {وَفِي عَادٍ، وَفِي ثَمُودَ، وَفِي موسى}: the like of it was mentioned earlier.

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ جَعَلَتْهُ كالرميم}: this clause is in the position of the second object of «تَذَرُ», as if it were said: "it leaves nothing but made so", like «ما تركتُ زيداً إلاَّ عالماً» ("I left Zayd only as a scholar"). The Shaykh parsed it as a ḥāl (circumstantial), which is not clear.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {الصاعقة}: this is the reading of the majority. Al-Kisāʾī read «الصَّعْقَة», and al-Ḥasan «الصاقِعة». All of this was mentioned in al-Baqara.
His saying: {وَهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the object. «ينظرون» was said to be from «النظر» (looking), and also from «الانتظار» (waiting), that is, "they were awaiting the punishment promised them".

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ}: The two (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Abū ʿAmr read it with genitive on the «ميم»; the rest read it accusative. Abū al-Sammāl, Ibn Miqsam and Abū ʿAmr in the transmission of al-Aṣmaʿī read «وقومُ» nominative. As for the genitive, there are four views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to «وفي الأرض». The second: that it is conjoined to «وفي موسى». The third: that it is conjoined to «وفي عاد». The fourth: that it is conjoined to «وفي ثمودَ», and this is the apparent one because of its nearness and the distance of the others. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else, for he said: "It was read with genitive in the sense of «وفي قوم نوح»." This is strengthened by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, «وفي قوم نوح». Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned only the last view because of its clarity.
As for the accusative, there are six views. The first: that it is accusative by an implied verb, that is, «وأهلَكْنا قومَ نوح» ("and we destroyed the people of Nūḥ"), because what precedes indicates it. The second: that it is accusative by an implied «اذْكُرْ»; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned only these two. The third: that it is accusative as a conjunction on the object of «فأَخَذْناه». The fourth: that it is conjoined to the object of {فَنَبَذْنَاهُمْ فِي اليم}, and what fits this is that the people of Nūḥ were drowned before; but it is problematic, as they were not drowned in the sea (yamm), and the basis of conjunction is that it requires sharing in the attached elements. The fifth: that it is conjoined to the object of «فَأَخَذَتْهم الصاعقةُ»; and in it is a problem, because the thunderbolt did not seize them, rather they were destroyed by drowning, unless by «الصاعقة» is meant the calamity and great visitation of whatever kind, in which case it comes close. The sixth: that it is conjoined to the position of «وفي موسى»; Abū al-Baqāʾ reported it, and it is weak.
As for the nominative, it is as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with an implied khabar (predicate), that is, «أهلَكْناهم». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The khabar is what comes after it", meaning His saying «إنهم كانوا قوماً فاسقين». It is not permissible that he mean His saying «من قبلُ», since the adverbial is incomplete and so cannot be predicated.

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying: {والسمآء بَنَيْنَاهَا}: The majority read it accusative on the basis of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb with a pronoun); likewise His saying {والأرضَ فَرَشْناها}. The implied sense: «وبَنَيْنا السماءَ بَنَيْناها». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "that is, «ورفَعْنا السماءَ»", so he implied the governor from a wording other than the overt one; this is resorted to only when an implication that agrees in wording is impossible, as in «زيداً مررت به» and «زيداً ضربْتُ غلامَه». But in a case like «زيداً ضربتُه», only «ضربْتُ زيداً» is implied. Abū al-Sammāl and Ibn Miqsam read both nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar being what comes after them. The accusative is preferred because the clause of ishtighāl is conjoined to a verbal clause before it.
His saying: {بِأَيْدٍ}: It is permissible that it be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial). There are two views on it: the first, that it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «بَنَيْناها», that is, "coupled with strength"; the second, that it is a ḥāl from its object, that is, "coupled with strength". It is also permissible that the «باء» be causal, that is, "by reason of our power"; and it is permissible that the «باء» be figuratively one of instrument, by making «الأَيْد» like the tool with which one builds, as in your saying «بَنَيْتُ بيتَك بالآجُرِّ» ("I built your house with brick").
His saying: {وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ}: It is permissible that the clause be a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «بَنَيْناها», and permissible that it be a ḥāl from its object; the object of «مُوْسِعون» is omitted, that is, "extending its structure". It is also permissible that no object be implied for it, because its meaning is «لَقادِرون» ("able"), from your saying «ما في وُسْعي كذا», that is, "it is not within my capacity and strength."

semin-durr:48-48.t: His saying: {فَنِعْمَ الماهدون}: the one specified for praise is omitted because the meaning is understood, that is, «نحن» ("we"), as in His saying {نِعْمَ العبد} [ص: 44].

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {وَمِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ}: It is permissible that it be attached to «خَلَقْنا», that is, "we created from everything two kinds"; and that it be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «زوجَيْن», because originally it is an adjective of it, the implied sense being "we created two kinds, existing from everything". The first is stronger in meaning.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {كَذَلِكَ}: There are two views. The more apparent: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, "the matter is like that". The pointing by «ذلك» is, al-Zamakhsharī said, "to their denial of the Messenger and calling him a sorcerer and a madman", then he explained what he had stated in general by "«ما أَتى»". The second: that the «كاف» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); Makkī said this and did not make clear its implied form. It is not valid for it to be accusative by what comes after it, because of the negative «ما». As for the meaning, it is not impossible, and for that reason al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is not valid for the «كاف» to be accusative by «أتى», because the negative «ما» does not allow what follows it to govern what precedes it; had it been «لم يأتِ», it would have been valid." He means that if «لم» had come in place of «ما», it would be permissible for the «كاف» to be accusative by «أتى», because the meaning allows it. The implied sense: "Quraysh denied with a denial like the denial of the earlier nations of their messengers." This is indicated by His saying {مَآ أَتَى الذين مِن قَبْلِهِمْ} to the end of the verse.
His saying: {إِلاَّ قَالُواْ}: the clause of saying is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from {الذين مِن قَبْلِهِمْ}, and «من رسولٍ» is the fāʿil (agent) of «أتى»; as if it were said: "No messenger came to the earlier ones except while they said: He is a sorcerer." The pronoun in «به» refers to the saying indicated by «قالوا», that is, "Did the earlier and the later ones bequeath this saying to one another, containing 'sorcerer or madman'?" The interrogative is for amazement.

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُونِ}: attached to «خَلَقْتُ». There was disagreement over the jinn and mankind: is the intent general, the meaning being "except to command them to worship and to have them acknowledge it"? This is reported from ʿAlī. Or the meaning is "to obey me and submit to my decree", so the believer does that willingly and the disbeliever unwillingly. Or the meaning is "except as prepared for worship", and then among them some can do it and some cannot, as in your saying «هذا القلمُ بَرَيْتُه للكتابة» ("I trimmed this pen for writing"), after which you may write with it or may not. Or the intent is specific, and the meaning is: "I did not create the jinn and the believing humans". It was also said: "the obedient". The first is best.

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {أَن يُطْعِمُونِ}: It was said that a muḍāf is omitted in it, that is, "that they feed my creation". It was also said that the meaning is "that they benefit me", and the expression used one of the forms of benefit, because it is the habit of masters to benefit from their servants, while Allah, glorified and exalted, is free of need of that.

semin-durr:58-58.t: His saying: {المتين}: The majority read it nominative. There are several views: either a naʿt (adjective) of «الرزَّاق», or a naʿt of «ذو», or a naʿt of the ism of «إنَّ» by position, which is the school of al-Jarmī, al-Farrāʾ and others, or a khabar after a khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. On every assumption it is emphasis, because «ذو القوة» gives the same benefit. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «الرازق», as he read «وَفِي السمآء رازِقُكُمْ», as mentioned. Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb and al-Aʿmash read «المتينِ» genitive; it was said: an adjective of «القوة», and its adjective was made masculine because its feminine is not a true feminine. It was also said: because it has the sense of «الأَيْد». Ibn Jinnī said: "It is genitive by proximity, as in their saying «هذا جُحْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ» ("this is the hole of a ruined lizard")", meaning that it is an adjective of a nominative word and was made genitive only because it neighboured a genitive. This is the less preferred view because another is possible, and proximity is not resorted to except in need.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying: {ذَنُوباً}: «الذَّنوب» originally is the bucket filled with water. In the hadith: «فأتى بذَنوبٍ من ماءٍ» ("then he was brought a bucket of water"). If it is not full, it is a «دَلْو»; then it was used to express a share. Alqama said:
4113 - وفي كلِّ حَيٍّ قد خبَطْتُ بنِعْمَةٍ ... فحُقَّ لشاسٍ مِنْ نَداكَ ذَنوبُ
(In every tribe I have dispensed a favour, so a share of your generosity is due to Shās.)
In the paucal plural it is «أَذْنِبة», and in the plural of abundance «ذَنائب». When this verse was recited, the king said: "Yes, and «أَذْنِبَة»." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الذَّنوب» is the large bucket. This is a figure of speech, its origin being among water-drawers who share the water, so this one has a bucket and that one has a bucket. The rajaz poet said:
4114 - لنا ذَنوبٌ ولكم ذَنُوبُ ... فإنْ أَبَيْتُمْ فلنا القَليبُ
(We have a bucket and you have a bucket; if you refuse, then the well is ours.)
Al-Rāghib said: «الذَّنوب» is the bucket that has a tail (dhanab)." End. He thereby took account of the derivation. «الذَّنوب» is also a horse with a long tail, which is an attribute on the pattern «فَعُوْل»; and «الذَّنوب» is the meat of the lower back. It is said: «يومٌ ذَنوبٌ», that is, a day of long evil, by metaphor from that.

semin-durr:60-60.t: His saying: {الذي يُوعَدُونَ}: the returning pronoun is omitted, because its conditions are fulfilled, that is, «يُوْعَدُونه».

ukberi-tibyan:1-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالذَّارِيَاتِ ذَرْوًا (١) فَالْحَامِلَاتِ وِقْرًا (٢) فَالْجَارِيَاتِ يُسْرًا (٣) فَالْمُقَسِّمَاتِ أَمْرًا (٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَرْوًا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) governed by the active participle. And (وِقْرًا) is the mafʿūl (object) of «الْحَامِلَاتِ». And (يُسْرًا) is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "made easy". And (أَمْرًا) is the mafʿūl of «الْمُقَسِّمَاتِ».

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ (١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَ هُمْ): it is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is annexed to a clause, and its position is nominative, i.e. "it is the day when they …".
It is also said that it is declinable, and was given fatḥa according to the rule of the adverb (ẓarf). It is also said that its position is accusative, i.e. "I mean their day".
It is also said that it is an adverb for الدِّين, i.e. "the day of recompense". It is also said that the implied wording is "they will be recompensed on the day when they …".
And (هُمْ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يُفْتَنُونَ» is the khabar (predicate); He made it transitive with عَلَى because the meaning is "they are forced onto the Fire".
It is also said that it means فِي.

ukberi-tibyan:15-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ (١٥) آخِذِينَ مَا آتَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ مُحْسِنِينَ (١٦)).
And (آخِذِينَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the adverbial phrase, and the adverbial phrase is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ.
If it is asked: how did the adverbial phrase come here as the khabar and «آخِذِينَ» as a ḥāl, while the reverse is the case in His saying: (إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي عَذَابِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدُونَ)?
The answer is: the khabar is what the clause is aimed at, and the purpose of mentioning the criminals is to inform of their being made to abide forever, because a believer may be in the Fire but will come out of it. As for «إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ …», the adverbial phrase was made the khabar in it because they are safe from coming out of it, so آخِذِينَ was made an extra (faḍla) element.

ukberi-tibyan:17-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَانُوا قَلِيلًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ مَا يَهْجَعُونَ (١٧) وَبِالْأَسْحَارِ هُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ (١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَانُوا قَلِيلًا): regarding the khabar (predicate) of «كَانَ» there are two views.
First: it is «مَا يَهْجَعُونَ»; and on this view there are two views regarding «مَا». One: it is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "they used to sleep little", and «قَلِيلًا» is a naʿt (adjective) of an adverb or of a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a little time" or "a little sleep".
The other: it is negating; some grammarians mentioned this, and it was rejected against him, because what lies within the scope of a negation cannot precede it, and «قَلِيلًا» is within its scope.
The second view: (قَلِيلًا) is the khabar of كَانَ, and (مَا) is maṣdariyya (infinitival), i.e. "their sleep was little", as you say: "their sleep used to be scant".
On this view «مَا يَهْجَعُونَ» may also be a badal (substitute) for the noun of كَانَ, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl).
And (مِنَ اللَّيْلِ) may not be attached to «يَهْجَعُونَ» on this view, because that would involve putting what the maṣdar governs before it; rather it is accusative by way of clarification (tabyīn), i.e. it is attached to an omitted verb which يَهْجَعُونَ explains. Some of them said: the speech is complete at His saying «قَلِيلًا», then He began anew, saying: مِنَ اللَّيْلِ مَا يَهْجَعُونَ. This is far-fetched, because if you make «مَا» negating, it is unsound for the reason we mentioned; and if you make it maṣdariyya, there is no praise in it, because all people sleep at night. (وَبِالْأَسْحَارِ): the bāʾ means فِي.

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَفِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَفَلَا تُبْصِرُونَ (٢١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَفِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ): the mubtadaʾ (subject) is omitted, i.e. "and in yourselves there are signs"; whoever makes (the noun) nominative by the adverbial phrase puts the pronoun of the signs in the adverbial phrase.
It is also said that it is attached to «تُبْصِرُونَ»; this is weak, because the interrogative and the fāʾ prevent that.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَفِي السَّمَاءِ رِزْقُكُمْ وَمَا تُوعَدُونَ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَفِي السَّمَاءِ رِزْقُكُمْ), i.e. the cause of your provision, meaning the rain.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَوَرَبِّ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ مِثْلَ مَا أَنَّكُمْ تَنْطِقُونَ (٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِثْلَ مَا): it is read in the nominative, as a naʿt (adjective) of «حَقٌّ», or as a second khabar (predicate), or on the basis that both form a single khabar, like "sweet-sour" (حُلْوٌ حَامِضٌ). And «مَا» is redundant (zāʾida) on all three views.
It is also read with fatḥa, and in it there are two views. First: it is declinable; then on this view there are several views on its accusative: either it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the indefinite noun, or from the pronoun in it; or it is by an implied "I mean" (أَعْنِي); or it is nominative in position but was given fatḥa just as the adverb was given fatḥa in His saying: (لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ), according to the view of al-Akhfash; and «مَا» on these views is also redundant. The second view: it is indeclinable (mabnī), and regarding how it is made indeclinable there are two views.
One: it was compounded with «مَا», like خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ ("fifteen"); and «مَا» on this view may be redundant, or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective. The other: it was made indeclinable because it was annexed to something vague (mubham) and has vagueness in itself; the like of it has been mentioned at His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمِنْ خِزْيِ يَوْمِئِذٍ). On this view too, «مَا» is either redundant or means "a thing".
As for «أَنَّكُمْ», its position may be genitive by annexation if «مَا» is made redundant, or it may be a badal (substitute) for it if it means "a thing"; it may also be in the position of the accusative by an implied "I mean", or of the nominative on the implied wording "it is that you …".

ukberi-tibyan:24-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ (٢٤) إِذْ دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُوا سَلَامًا قَالَ سَلَامٌ قَوْمٌ مُنْكَرُونَ (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ دَخَلُوا): «إِذْ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for حَدِيث, or for ضَيْف, or for مُكْرَمِين; not for أَتَاكَ. The discussion of «سَلَامًا» has been given in Hūd.

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَقْبَلَتِ امْرَأَتُهُ فِي صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ قَالُوا كَذَلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ (٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي صَرَّةٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent.
And (كَذَلِكَ) is in the position of the accusative by the second «قَالَ».

ukberi-tibyan:33-34.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِنُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ حِجَارَةً مِنْ طِينٍ (٣٣) مُسَوَّمَةً عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ (٣٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُسَوَّمَةً) is a naʿt (adjective) of حِجَارَة, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition phrase.
And (عِنْدَ) is an adverb (ẓarf) for مُسَوَّمَة.

ukberi-tibyan:38-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَفِي مُوسَى إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَاهُ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ بِسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ (٣٨) فَتَوَلَّى بِرُكْنِهِ وَقَالَ سَاحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ (٣٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَفِي مُوسَى), i.e. "and We left in Moses a sign".
And (إِذْ) is an adverb (ẓarf) for آيَة, or for تَرَكْنَا, or an adjective (naʿt) of it. And (بِسُلْطَانٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from مُوسَى, or from his pronoun.
And (بِرُكْنِهِ) is a ḥāl from the pronoun of Pharaoh.

ukberi-tibyan:41-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَفِي عَادٍ إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّيحَ الْعَقِيمَ (٤١) مَا تَذَرُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ أَتَتْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا جَعَلَتْهُ كَالرَّمِيمِ (٤٢) وَفِي ثَمُودَ إِذْ قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَمَتَّعُوا حَتَّى حِينٍ (٤٣)).
(وَفِي عَادٍ); (وَفِي ثَمُودَ), i.e. "and We left a sign".

ukberi-tibyan:46-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمًا فَاسِقِينَ (٤٦) وَالسَّمَاءَ بَنَيْنَاهَا بِأَيْدٍ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ (٤٧) وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَاهَا فَنِعْمَ الْمَاهِدُونَ (٤٨) وَمِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ (٤٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ): it is read in the genitive, conjoined to ثَمُود.
And in the accusative on the implied wording "and We destroyed", indicated by the earlier mention of the destruction of the nations named; it may also be conjoined to the position of «وَفِي مُوسَى».
And in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being what follows it; or on the implied wording "they were destroyed".
(وَالسَّمَاءَ) is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and We raised the heaven"; this is stronger than the nominative, because it is conjoined to something governed by a verb. «وَالْأَرْضَ» is like it.
And (بِأَيْدٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the verb [Translator's note: so in the source; perhaps "from the agent" is meant]. And (نِعْمَ الْمَاهِدُونَ), i.e. "We (are)"; the specified object of praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) was omitted.
(وَمِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خَلَقْنَا». It may also be a naʿt (adjective) of «زَوْجَيْنِ» that was put first and so became a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَذَلِكَ مَا أَتَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا قَالُوا سَاحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ (٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكَ), i.e. "the matter is thus".

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَتِينُ (٥٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْمَتِينُ): in the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of Allah, glorified is He.
It is also said that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He is the Firm"; here it is an allusion (kināya) to the meaning of strength, since its meaning is might in seizing; and this is in the sense of the reading with the genitive. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَنْ أُفِكَ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ): the hāʾ refers back to the religion (al-dīn), or to «مَا تُوعَدُونَ».
It is also said: to «قَوْلٍ مُخْتَلِفٍ», i.e. "turned away from that is whoever is turned away from the truth".

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat "al-Dhāriyāt".
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والذّارِياتِ ذَرْوًا﴾: It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that Ibn al-Kawwāʾ asked him about ﴿والذّارِياتِ ذَرْوًا﴾, and ʿAlī said: "They are the winds." He said: ﴿فالحامِلاتِ وِقْرًا﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 2]? He said: "The clouds." He said: ﴿فالجارِياتِ يُسْرًا﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 3]? He said: "The ships." He said: ﴿فالمُقَسِّماتِ أمْرًا﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 4]? He said: "The angels." And all the exegetes hold ʿAlī's view on this.
[Translator's note: the source reads «الكَوّاءَ»; the questioner is usually named ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Kawwāʾ.]
﴿والذّارِياتِ﴾ is genitive (majrūr) by the oath; the meaning is: "I swear by the scattering winds" and by these things, and the answer is: ﴿إنَّما تُوعَدُونَ لَصادِقٌ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 5]. Some said: the meaning is: "and by the Lord of the scattering winds", as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَوَرَبِّ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ إنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 23]. "اَلذّارِياتُ" is from "ذَرَتِ الرِّيحُ، تَذْرُو", when the wind scatters dust and other things. One says "ذَرَتِ الرِّيحُ" and "أذْرَتْ" with one meaning: "ذَرَتْ، فَهي ذارِيَةٌ، وهُنَّ ذارِياتٌ", and "أذْرَتْ، فَهي مُذْرِيَةٌ" and "مُذْرِياتٌ" for the plural, and "ذارِياتٌ" as well. The meaning is: "By the Lord of the scattering winds, the Lord of the running ships, and the Lord of the apportioning angels, what you are promised is true."

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُتِلَ الخَرّاصُونَ﴾: they are the liars; you say: "قَدْ تَخَرَّصَ عَلَيَّ فُلانٌ الباطِلَ" (so-and-so fabricated falsehood against me). It is also possible that "اَلْخَرّاصُونَ" are those who conjecture something without establishing it, and so act on what they do not know to be sound.

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَسْألُونَ أيّانَ يَوْمُ الدِّينِ﴾ — and "إيّانَ" is permissible, with kasra on the hamza as well as with fatḥa — that is: they say: when is the Day of Recompense?

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ هم عَلى النّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ﴾, with "يَوْمَ" in the accusative; and "يَوْمُ هم عَلى النّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ" (nominative) is permissible. Whoever puts it in the accusative, it is in two ways. One of them is in the sense of: "the recompense will occur on the day they are tried over the Fire". It is also possible that its form is the form of the accusative while its sense is the sense of the nominative, because it is in iḍāfa (annexed) to a whole clause. You say: "يُعْجِبُنِي يَوْمَ أنْتَ قائِمٌ" (the day you are standing pleases me), "يَوْمُ أنْتَ قائِمٌ" and "يَوْمُ أنْتَ تَقُومُ"; and if you wish you give it fatḥa while it is in the position of the nominative, as the poet said:
؎لَمْ يَمْنَعِ الشُّرْبَ مِنها غَيْرَ أنْ نَطَقَتْ ∗∗∗ حَمامَةٌ في غُصُونٍ ذاتِ أوْقالِ
(Nothing kept her from drinking but that a dove cooed among branches bearing dry fruit.)
It has also been transmitted as "غَيْرُ أنْ نَطَقَتْ". When he annexed "غَيْرُ" to "أنْ", which is not fully declinable (mutamakkin), it took fatḥa; likewise when "يَوْمُ" was annexed to "هم عَلى النّارِ", it took fatḥa. And as it has been read: "وَمِن خِزْيِ يَوْمَئْذٍ", where you give "يَوْمَ" fatḥa while it is in the position of the genitive, because you have annexed it to something not fully declinable. The meaning of ﴿يُفْتَنُونَ﴾ is: they are burned and punished. From that the black stones that look as though they have been burned by fire are called "اَلْفَتِينُ".

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ المُتَّقِينَ في جَنّاتٍ وعُيُونٍ﴾ ﴿آخِذِينَ ما آتاهم رَبُّهُمْ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 16]: He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known what the people of the Fire will have, then made known what the people of the Garden will have; because when He said: ﴿وَإنَّ الدِّينَ لَواقِعٌ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 6], He made known the recompense of the people of the Garden and the recompense of the people of the Fire.
His saying: ﴿آخِذِينَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 16] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning is: "the God-fearing are in gardens and springs, in the state of taking what their Lord has given them". Were it outside the Qur'an, "آخِذُونَ" (nominative) would be permissible, but the Muṣḥaf is not to be contradicted; the meaning would then be: "the God-fearing are taking what their Lord has given them, in gardens and springs". The first aspect is better in meaning, and the reading is according to it.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كانُوا قَلِيلا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ ما يَهْجَعُونَ﴾: the meaning is: "they used to slumber a little of the night", that is: "they used to sleep a little of the night". Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known in what their wakefulness consisted, and said: ﴿وَبِالأسْحارِ هم يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 18]. It is possible that "ما" is emphatic, redundant (laghw); and it is possible that "ما" with what follows it is a maṣdar (verbal noun; i.e. an interpreted maṣdar), so that the meaning is: "little of the night was their slumber".

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿وَفِي أمْوالِهِمْ حَقٌّ لِلسّائِلِ والمَحْرُومِ﴾: "اَلْمَحْرُومُ" (the deprived): it has come in the tafsīr (exegesis): the one whose wealth does not grow (lā yanmū); and more common in the language is lā yanmī lahu māl. It has also come that he is "اَلْمُجازِفُ" (the venturer), who scarcely earns anything.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿فَوَرَبِّ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ إنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ﴾, that is: "what the Prophet ﷺ brought is true, and His saying ﴿وَفِي السَّماءِ رِزْقُكم وما تُوعَدُونَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 22] is true". So the meaning is that what we have mentioned concerning the signs, provision and the affair of the Prophet ﷺ is true, ﴿مِثْلَ ما أنَّكم تَنْطِقُونَ﴾ — and it has been read "مِثْلُ ما أنَّكم تَنْطِقُونَ" (nominative). This is as you say in ordinary speech: "إنَّ هَذا لَحَقٌّ، كَما أنَّكَ مُتَكَلِّمٌ" (this is surely true, just as you are speaking). Whoever puts "مِثْلُ" in the nominative, it is a ṣifa (adjective) of al-ḥaqq, the meaning being: "it is surely a truth like your speaking". Whoever puts it in the accusative, it is of two kinds. One of them is that it is in the position of the nominative, except that, when it was annexed to "أنَّ", it took fatḥa. It is also possible that it is accusative for emphasis (tawkīd), in the sense of: "it is surely true, truly, like your speaking".

zajjaj:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿هَلْ أتاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إبْراهِيمَ المُكْرَمِينَ﴾: It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that when the angels came to him, he honoured them with the calf. It was also said: he honoured them by serving them himself — the blessings of Allah be upon him and upon them.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
﴿فَقالُوا سَلامًا قالَ سَلامٌ﴾ — and it has been read: "قالَ سِلْمٌ". The accusative of the first is in the sense of "peace be upon you, a greeting of peace" and "we greet you with a greeting of peace". Whoever reads ﴿قالَ سَلامٌ﴾, it is in two ways: in the sense of "he said: peace be upon you", and it is possible that it is in the sense of "our affair is peace". Whoever reads "سِلْمٌ", the meaning is: "he said: peace", that is: "my affair is peace" and "our affair is peace", that is: "there is no harm upon us".
His saying: ﴿قَوْمٌ مُنْكَرُونَ﴾: its nominative is in the sense of: "you are a people unknown".

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿فَراغَ إلى أهْلِهِ فَجاءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ﴾: the meaning of ﴿فَراغَ إلى أهْلِهِ﴾ is: he turned aside to them in such a way that they did not know why he had turned aside. Likewise one says: "راغَ فُلانٌ عَنّا" (so-and-so slipped away from us) when he turns away from them without their knowing.

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿فَقَرَّبَهُ إلَيْهِمْ قالَ ألا تَأْكُلُونَ﴾: the meaning is: "he brought it near to them so that they might eat of it, but they did not eat; he said: Will you not eat?!", as a disapproval, that is: "your conduct in not eating is something I find strange."

zajjaj:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأوْجَسَ مِنهم خِيفَةً قالُوا لا تَخَفْ﴾: the meaning of "أوْجَسَ" is: fear arose in his soul.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلامٍ عَلِيمٍ﴾: the meaning of "عَلِيمٍ" is that he will reach maturity and know.

zajjaj:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأقْبَلَتِ امْرَأتُهُ في صَرَّةٍ﴾: "اَلصَّرَّةُ" here is intense crying out. ﴿فَصَكَّتْ وجْهَها﴾, that is: she struck her face.
﴿وَقالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ﴾: the meaning is: "she said: I am a barren old woman, so how shall I give birth?!" The proof of that is His saying in another place: ﴿قالَتْ يا ويْلَتى أألِدُ وأنا عَجُوزٌ وهَذا بَعْلِي شَيْخًا﴾ [Hūd: 72]

zajjaj:30-30.t: ﴿قالُوا كَذَلِكَ قالَ رَبُّكِ﴾, that is: as we have said to you, so your Lord has said; that is: "we are only informing you on behalf of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and Allah is Wise, Knowing; He is able to make the barren one fertile, and the old woman likewise." So Abraham knew that they were messengers and that they were angels.

zajjaj:31-31.t: ﴿قالَ فَما خَطْبُكم أيُّها المُرْسَلُونَ﴾, that is: "what is your business? And for what have you been sent?"

zajjaj:32-32.t:
﴿قالُوا إنّا أُرْسِلْنا إلى قَوْمٍ مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ ﴿لِنُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ حِجارَةً مِن طِينٍ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 33], that is: "we have been sent to a criminal people to destroy them for their disbelief.
[Translator's note: the opening quotation mark in the source is not closed.]

zajjaj:34-34.t: ﴿مُسَوَّمَةً عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾, that is: marked; on every stone of them is the name of the one whose destruction was appointed by it. "اَلْمُسَوَّمَةُ" is the marked one, taken from "اَلسُّومَةُ", which is the mark.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ الدِّينَ لَواقِعٌ﴾, that is: "the recompense for your deeds will surely come to pass".

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿والسَّماءِ ذاتِ الحُبُكِ﴾ ﴿إنَّكم لَفي قَوْلٍ مُخْتَلِفٍ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 8]: It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that it is the one possessing good khuluq. [Translator's note: the source reads «الخُلُقِ» (character); «الخَلْقِ» (form, make) is likely intended.] The people of the language say: "ذاتِ الحُبُكِ" means possessing fine pathways. "اَلْمَحْبُوكُ" in the language is that whose making is done well; and every [pattern of] pathways you see in water and in sand when the wind strikes it is "حُبُكٌ". Its singular is "حِباكٌ", like "مِثالٌ" and "مُثُلٌ"; and its singular may also be "حَبِيكَةٌ", like "طَرِيقَةٌ" and "طُرُقٌ".
His saying: ﴿إنَّكم لَفي قَوْلٍ مُخْتَلِفٍ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 8], that is: concerning the affair of the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَن أُفِكَ﴾, that is: turned away from it is whoever is turned away.

zajjaj:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿وَتَرَكْنا فِيها آيَةً لِلَّذِينَ يَخافُونَ العَذابَ الألِيمَ﴾, that is: We left in the city of the people of Lot a sign for those who fear, showing them that Allah destroyed them, so that others might be deterred from doing what they did.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَفِي مُوسى إذْ أرْسَلْناهُ إلى فِرْعَوْنَ بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾: this is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to His saying: ﴿وَفِي الأرْضِ آياتٌ لِلْمُوقِنِينَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 20], and to His saying: ﴿وَتَرَكْنا فِيها آيَةً لِلَّذِينَ يَخافُونَ العَذابَ الألِيمَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 37].
His saying: ﴿بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾, that is: with a clear proof.

zajjaj:39-39.t: ﴿فَتَوَلّى بِرُكْنِهِ﴾, that is: he turned away with that by which he strengthened himself, of his troops and his dominion. ﴿وَقالَ ساحِرٌ أوْ مَجْنُونٌ﴾: the meaning is: "and he said: this is a sorcerer or a madman".

zajjaj:40-40.t: ﴿فَأخَذْناهُ وجُنُودَهُ فَنَبَذْناهم في اليَمِّ﴾: "So We seized him and his support by which he strengthened himself". ﴿فَنَبَذْناهم في اليَمِّ﴾: "اَلْيَمُّ" is the sea. ﴿وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ﴾, that is: blame clings to him; that is: what was done to him is not an expiation for him. "اَلْمُلِيمُ" in the language is one who does what he deserves to be blamed for. The meaning of "نَبَذْناهم" is: We cast them; everything you cast away you say of it: "قَدْ نَبَذْتُهُ" (I have cast it). From that is "نَبَذْتُ النَّبِيذَ" (I steeped the nabīdh), and from that you call a foundling "مَنبُوذٌ", because he has been thrown away.

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿وَفِي عادٍ إذْ أرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّيحَ العَقِيمَ﴾, that is: "and in ʿĀd too there is a sign", according to what we explained concerning His saying ﴿وَفِي مُوسى﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 38]. The barren wind is the one with which there is no fertilisation, that is: it does not bring rain; it is only a wind of destruction.

zajjaj:42-42.t: ﴿ما تَذَرُ مِن شَيْءٍ أتَتْ عَلَيْهِ إلا جَعَلَتْهُ كالرَّمِيمِ﴾: "اَلرَّمِيمُ" is dry, crumbled leaves, like hashīm (dry stubble), as He said: ﴿كَهَشِيمِ المُحْتَظِرِ﴾ [al-Qamar: 31]

zajjaj:43-43.t: ﴿وَفِي ثَمُودَ﴾, that is: and in Thamūd too there is a sign.

zajjaj:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِن قَبْلُ﴾: it has been read "وَقَوْمِ نُوحٍ" in the genitive and "وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ" in the accusative. Whoever puts it in the genitive, the meaning is: "and in the people of Noah". Whoever puts it in the accusative, it is conjoined to the sense of His saying: ﴿فَأخَذَتْهُمُ الصّاعِقَةُ وهم يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 44]; the meaning of "أخَذَتْهُمُ الصّاعِقَةُ" is: We destroyed them, so the meaning is: "We destroyed them, and We destroyed the people of Noah before". The better — and Allah knows best — is that it be construed on His saying: ﴿فَأخَذْناهُ وجُنُودَهُ فَنَبَذْناهم في اليَمِّ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 40], because the meaning is: "We drowned him and his troops, and We drowned the people of Noah before".

zajjaj:47-47.t: ﴿والسَّماءَ بَنَيْناها بِأيْدٍ﴾, that is: with strength. ﴿وَإنّا لَمُوسِعُونَ﴾: We have made between it and the earth an expanse.

zajjaj:48-48.t: ﴿والأرْضَ فَرَشْناها﴾ is conjoined to what precedes it, accusative by an implied (muḍmar) verb; the meaning is: "and We spread the earth — We spread it". The meaning of ﴿فَنِعْمَ الماهِدُونَ﴾ is "[excellent spreaders are] We", but the wording in His saying "فَرَشْناها" indicates the implied, omitted element.

zajjaj:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿وَمِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنا زَوْجَيْنِ﴾: the meaning — and Allah knows best — relates to animals, because the male and the female are called "زَوْجانِ" (a pair); like it is ﴿وَأنَّهُ خَلَقَ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ والأُنْثى﴾ [al-Najm: 45]. It is also possible that the pair is from every thing, so that the meaning is: "in every thing — in animals the male and the female", and in other than them "two kinds, the origin of every living and lifeless thing" — and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:50-50.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَفِرُّوا إلى اللَّهِ﴾: the meaning is: "so flee to Allah from associating partners with Allah and from disobeying Him, to Him". ﴿إنِّي لَكم مِنهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾, that is: "I warn you of His punishment and His penalty".

zajjaj:51-51.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَجْعَلُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ إلَهًا آخَرَ إنِّي لَكم مِنهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ ﴿كَذَلِكَ ما أتى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ مِن رَسُولٍ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 52]: the meaning is: "the matter is thus", that is: as those before them did in denying the messengers.
﴿إلا قالُوا ساحِرٌ أوْ مَجْنُونٌ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 52], that is: "but they said: this is a sorcerer". "ساحِرٌ" is nominative by an implied "هُوَ" (he).

zajjaj:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿أتَواصَوْا بِهِ﴾: its meaning is: the first of them enjoined it upon the last of them. This is the alif of rebuke and the alif of interrogation.

zajjaj:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهم فَما أنْتَ بِمَلُومٍ﴾, that is: "there is no blame upon you, since you have delivered the message".

zajjaj:55-55.t: ﴿وَذَكِّرْ فَإنَّ الذِّكْرى تَنْفَعُ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, that is: remind them of the days of Allah, His punishment, His penalty and His mercy.

zajjaj:56-56.t: His saying: ﴿وَما خَلَقْتُ الجِنَّ والإنْسَ إلا لِيَعْبُدُونِ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, knew before He created the jinn and mankind who would worship Him, as distinct from those who would disbelieve in Him. Had He created them only to compel them to worship Him, they would all have been worshipping believers, and there would have been none among them who went astray and disbelieved. So the meaning is: "I did not create the jinn and mankind except to call them to My worship, and I will worship from them" — meaning from those who are its people.

zajjaj:57-57.t: ﴿ما أُرِيدُ مِنهم مِن رِزْقٍ وما أُرِيدُ أنْ يُطْعِمُونِ﴾, that is: I do not want them to provide for any of My servants, nor do I want them to feed him, because I am the Provider, the One who feeds.

zajjaj:58-58.t: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ هو الرَّزّاقُ ذُو القُوَّةِ المَتِينُ﴾: the reading is the nominative, and in Arabic it is better, with "اَلْمَتِينُ" being nominative as a ṣifa (adjective) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. Whoever reads "ذُو القُوَّةِ المَتِينِ", in the genitive, makes "اَلْمَتِينِ" a ṣifa of al-quwwa (strength), because the femininity of al-quwwa is like the femininity of al-mawʿiẓa, as He said: ﴿فَمَن جاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ﴾ [al-Baqara: 275], the meaning being: "whoever has received an admonition (waʿẓ)". The meaning of ﴿ذُو القُوَّةِ المَتِينُ﴾ is: Possessor of intense power.

zajjaj:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ذَنُوبًا مِثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أصْحابِهِمْ﴾: "اَلذَّنُوبُ" in the language is a share, and the bucket is called "اَلذَّنُوبُ". The meaning is: "those who have done wrong will have a share of punishment like the share of their companions who were destroyed, such as ʿĀd, Thamūd and the people of Lot.
﴿فَلا يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾, that is: "if they are deferred until the Day of Resurrection".
[Translator's note: the quotation marks in the source are not balanced here.]

zajjaj:60-60.t: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن يَوْمِهِمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ﴾, that is: from the Day of Resurrection.
